A slight displacement lowers its center of gravity permanently
records.explanation: Correct: In stable equilibrium, when slightly displaced, the centre of gravity rises and a restoring force brings the body back to its original position. A is wrong because a high centre of gravity actually promotes instability, not stability. C is wrong because the centre of gravity remaining at the same height after displacement describes neutral equilibrium instead. D is wrong because a permanent lowering of the centre of gravity after displacement describes unstable equilibrium.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The equilibrant of two forces is
options: Equal in magnitude and same in direction as their resultant
The vector sum of the two forces
Equal in magnitude but opposite in direction to their resultant
The difference between the two forces
records.explanation: Correct: The equilibrant is the single force that, when added to the given forces, produces equilibrium — it has the same magnitude as the resultant but acts in the opposite direction. A is wrong because equal magnitude in the same direction would double the resultant rather than balance it. B is wrong because the vector sum IS the resultant itself, not the equilibrant. D is wrong because the difference has neither the correct magnitude nor direction in general.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A machine has an efficiency of 80% and a velocity ratio of 5. Its mechanical advantage is
records.explanation: Correct: Efficiency = (Mechanical Advantage / Velocity Ratio) × 100%. 80 = (MA/5) × 100, so MA = (80 × 5)/100 = 4. A is wrong because 6.25 = VR/Efficiency inverts the correct relationship. C is wrong because 0.16 = Efficiency/VR uses the wrong operation. D is wrong because 25 = VR × Efficiency (5 × 5) applies the wrong operation entirely.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A 60 W bulb is used for 10 hours daily. The electrical energy consumed in 30 days (in kWh) is
records.explanation: Correct: Energy = Power × Time = 60 W × (10 × 30) hours = 60 × 300 = 18,000 Wh = 18 kWh. B is wrong because it effectively uses 600W instead of 60W. C is wrong because it's off by a factor of 100. D is wrong because it divides instead of multiplying by the total hours.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A car engine exerts a force of 2000 N and moves at 20 ms⁻¹. The power of the engine is
records.explanation: Correct: Power = Force × velocity = 2000 × 20 = 40,000 W = 40 kW. B is wrong because 100 W = F/v divides instead of multiplying. C is wrong because 400 kW comes from a misplaced decimal. D is wrong because 4 W has no basis in the calculation.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A body of mass 2 kg falls from rest through 5 m. Its kinetic energy just before hitting the ground is (g = 10 ms⁻²)
records.explanation: Correct: By conservation of energy, KE = loss in PE = mgh = 2 × 10 × 5 = 100 J, since all potential energy converts to kinetic energy. B is wrong because 50 J uses only ½mgh, missing the full PE value. C is wrong because 200 J = 2mgh doubles the correct value. D is wrong because 10 J = mh omits g entirely.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The principle of conservation of energy states that
options: Energy can be created but not destroyed
Energy can be destroyed but not created
The total amount of energy in an isolated system remains constant
Kinetic energy always equals potential energy
records.explanation: Correct: The law of conservation of energy states that energy can neither be created nor destroyed but can be converted from one form to another, so the total energy of an isolated system stays constant. A is wrong because energy cannot be created — this violates the law. B is wrong because energy also cannot be destroyed — this also violates the law. D is wrong because KE = PE only at specific points during motion; it's the total (KE + PE) that's conserved, not the individual amounts.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Solar energy is classified as a renewable energy source because
options: It is continuously replenished by the sun and will not run out in human timescales
records.explanation: Correct: Renewable energy sources are naturally replenished and not depleted with use; solar energy comes directly from the sun, which will continue shining for billions of years. A is wrong because solar energy cannot actually be stored indefinitely — it must be converted and stored, e.g. in batteries. B is wrong because solar energy does produce heat, as used by solar thermal panels. D is wrong because cost has nothing to do with whether a source is classified as renewable.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The area under a force-distance graph represents
records.explanation: Correct: Work = ∫F·ds, so the area under a force-distance (F-x) graph equals the work done by the force over that displacement. A is wrong because power = work/time, which isn't directly read from an F-x graph's area. C is wrong because acceleration requires force and mass (a = F/m), not derivable this way. D is wrong because momentum involves mass and velocity, unrelated to a force-distance graph.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Static friction is always GREATER than kinetic (dynamic) friction because
options: Static surfaces have more area of contact
Intermolecular adhesive forces are stronger when surfaces are not sliding
records.explanation: Correct: When surfaces are at rest relative to each other, molecular adhesion bonds build up, requiring a larger force to break and initiate motion; once sliding begins, fewer bonds form simultaneously. A is wrong because friction is largely independent of contact area, per Amontons' laws. C is wrong because standard kinetic friction is approximately independent of velocity. D is wrong because roughness affects both types of friction equally — static exceeds kinetic due to adhesion, not roughness.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A ball bearing falling through oil reaches terminal velocity when
options: Its weight equals the viscous drag plus upthrust
The viscous drag force equals zero
records.explanation: Correct: Terminal velocity is reached when the net force is zero, i.e. Weight = Upthrust + Viscous drag (per Stokes' law: F = 6πηrv); no net force means no acceleration, giving constant velocity. B is wrong because at v = 0 the ball has just started falling, whereas terminal velocity is the maximum constant velocity. C is wrong because viscous drag is only zero when v = 0, not at terminal velocity. D is wrong because at terminal velocity, acceleration = 0, not maximum.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: According to Stokes' law, the viscous force on a sphere falling through a fluid is
records.explanation: Correct: Stokes' law states F = 6πηrv, where η is the coefficient of viscosity, r is the sphere's radius, and v is its velocity, applicable under laminar flow conditions. B is wrong because πηr²v has an incorrect dimensional structure. C is wrong because ηrv/6π inverts the constant term. D is wrong because η/rv has the wrong arrangement — v should be in the numerator.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Which of the following is NOT a way to reduce friction?
options: Increasing the normal force between surfaces
records.explanation: Correct: Since friction force F = μN, increasing the normal force N directly increases friction, unlike the other options, which all reduce it. A is wrong as an answer because lubrication does reduce friction by creating a fluid film between surfaces. B is wrong as an answer because ball bearings replace sliding friction with much smaller rolling friction. D is wrong as an answer because polishing reduces surface roughness and thus friction.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A machine with velocity ratio 8 and efficiency 75% is used to lift a 200 N load. The effort required is
records.explanation: Correct: Efficiency = (MA/VR) × 100. 75 = (MA/8) × 100, so MA = 6. Since MA = Load/Effort, 6 = 200/Effort, giving Effort = 200/6 = 33.3 N. B is wrong because 25 N assumes MA = 8, i.e. 100% efficiency. C is wrong because 1200 N = VR × Load confuses velocity ratio with inverse effort. D is wrong because 18.75 N results from an incorrect rearrangement of the formula.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Which class of lever has the effort between the fulcrum and the load?
records.explanation: Correct: In a Class 3 lever, the effort is positioned between the fulcrum and the load, as seen in tweezers or the forearm. A is wrong because Class 1 has the fulcrum between the load and effort, as in scissors or a seesaw. B is wrong because Class 2 has the load between the fulcrum and effort, as in a wheelbarrow. D is wrong because each class has a distinct arrangement, not a shared one.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Why is the efficiency of a machine always less than 100%?
options: Machines always gain more energy than they use
Energy is lost in overcoming friction and moving parts of the machine itself
Velocity ratio is always greater than mechanical advantage
The load always moves faster than the effort
records.explanation: Correct: In any real machine, some input energy is lost to friction between moving parts, to heat, and to moving the machine's own components, so useful output energy is always less than input energy. A is wrong because machines convert, not generate, energy — output can never exceed input. C is wrong because VR > MA is a consequence of inefficiency, not its cause. D is wrong because in most machines with MA > 1, the load actually moves slower than the effort point, not faster.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A spring of natural length 20 cm is extended by 5 cm when a force of 10 N is applied. The spring constant is
records.explanation: Correct: Hooke's law states F = ke, so k = F/e = 10 N / 0.05 m = 200 Nm⁻¹ (note that extension must be converted to metres). B is wrong because 2 Nm⁻¹ = F/e uses the extension in cm without proper unit conversion. C is wrong because 0.5 Nm⁻¹ inverts the formula (e/F instead of F/e). D is wrong because 50 Nm⁻¹ incorrectly uses e = 0.2 m, the total length, rather than just the extension.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The elastic limit of a material is the point beyond which
options: The extension is proportional to force
The material does not return to its original shape when the load is removed
records.explanation: Correct: Beyond the elastic limit, permanent deformation occurs, and the material enters the plastic region where it no longer obeys Hooke's law and doesn't fully recover its original shape. A is wrong because Hooke's law is obeyed BELOW the elastic limit, not beyond it. B is wrong because proportionality between extension and force also holds only BELOW the elastic limit. D is wrong because breaking occurs at the breaking point, which lies beyond the elastic limit — not at the limit itself.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The work done in stretching a spring by extension e with spring constant k is
records.explanation: Correct: Work done equals the area under the F-e graph = ½ × F × e = ½ × ke × e = ½ke², which represents the elastic potential energy stored in the spring. A is wrong because ke equals the force itself, not the work done. B is wrong because 2ke incorrectly doubles the force without proper derivation. D is wrong because ke² misses the ½ factor that comes from the triangular area under the graph.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Young's modulus is defined as the ratio of
records.explanation: Correct: Young's Modulus E = Stress/Strain = (F/A)/(e/L), which measures the stiffness of a material within the elastic region, with units of Nm⁻² or Pa. B is wrong because strain/stress is the compliance, the inverse of Young's modulus. C is wrong because force/area is simply stress, not Young's modulus. D is wrong because extension/original length is strain, only one component of the full ratio.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The pressure at a depth of 5 m in water is approximately (density of water = 1000 kgm⁻³, g = 10 ms⁻²)
records.explanation: Correct: Pressure P = ρgh = 1000 × 10 × 5 = 50,000 Pa = 50 kPa, the gauge pressure due to the water column alone. B is wrong because 5,000 Pa = ρg × 0.5 uses 0.5 m instead of the correct 5 m depth. C is wrong because 500,000 Pa is off by a factor of 10. D is wrong because 50 Pa omits both the density and g values entirely.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Pascal's principle states that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is
options: Transmitted equally to all parts of the fluid
Proportional to the depth of the fluid
records.explanation: Correct: Pascal's principle states that pressure exerted on a confined fluid is transmitted undiminished in all directions throughout the fluid, forming the basis of hydraulic machines. B is wrong because fluids transmit, rather than absorb, pressure. C is wrong because pressure proportional to depth describes hydrostatic pressure, a different property from Pascal's principle. D is wrong because pressure inversely proportional to volume actually describes Boyle's law for gases.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A hydraulic press has a small piston of area 10 cm² and a large piston of area 200 cm². If a force of 50 N is applied to the small piston, the force exerted by the large piston is
records.explanation: Correct: By Pascal's principle, F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂, so F₂ = F₁ × A₂/A₁ = 50 × 200/10 = 50 × 20 = 1000 N. B is wrong because 2.5 N inverts the area ratio used in the calculation. C is wrong because 500 N uses an incorrect ratio of 10 instead of 20. D is wrong because 250 N introduces an extraneous factor not justified by the setup.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A barometer can be used as an altimeter because
options: Atmospheric pressure decreases with increasing altitude in a measurable way
Mercury pressure increases at higher altitudes
records.explanation: Correct: Since atmospheric pressure decreases predictably with altitude, a calibrated barometer reading can be converted into an altitude measurement, which is how aircraft altimeters function. A is wrong because mercury's density changes only slightly with temperature, not altitude — this isn't the working principle. C is wrong because temperature change with altitude describes the lapse rate, not the altimeter's operating principle. D is wrong because mercury column pressure actually DECREASES at higher altitudes, since less atmospheric pressure supports less mercury.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A solid displaces 200 cm³ of water when fully submerged. The upthrust on the solid is (density of water = 1000 kgm⁻³, g = 10 ms⁻²)
records.explanation: Correct: Upthrust = weight of fluid displaced = ρVg = 1000 × 200×10⁻⁶ × 10 = 1000 × 0.0002 × 10 = 2 N. B is wrong because 20 N uses V = 2000 cm³ or an extra factor of 10. C is wrong because 0.2 N leaves V in cm³ instead of converting to m³, a unit error. D is wrong because 200 N omits g or uses the wrong volume conversion.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Archimedes' principle states that when a body is partially or fully immersed in a fluid, the upthrust equals
records.explanation: Correct: Archimedes' principle states that upthrust (buoyancy force) equals the weight of fluid displaced by the body, measured in newtons (a force), not volume. A is wrong because the body sinks or floats depending on whether its weight equals the upthrust — they're only equal when the body is floating. B is wrong because volume displaced is used to calculate upthrust, but is not itself the upthrust. D is wrong because density alone doesn't give the upthrust — volume and g are also required.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A ship floats because
options: Iron is less dense than water
The average density of the ship (including air spaces) is less than or equal to that of water
Sea water has high salt content
records.explanation: Correct: A ship floats because its large hollow structure, with air inside, gives it an average density less than water; by the law of flotation, it displaces water equal to its own weight. A is wrong because iron IS denser than water — a solid iron block would sink. C is wrong because weight alone doesn't determine floating — average density relative to water is what matters. D is wrong because salt increases water density, which helps buoyancy but isn't the actual reason ships float.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The temperature 37°C on the Kelvin scale is
records.explanation: Correct: K = °C + 273 = 37 + 273 = 310 K, which is also normal human body temperature. B is wrong because 236 K involves an incorrect subtraction. C is wrong because 37 K simply forgets to add 273. D is wrong because 373 K = 100 + 273 is the boiling point of water, not 37°C.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A thermometric property must
options: Vary linearly and measurably with temperature
Be a chemical property of matter
Remain constant over a temperature range
records.explanation: Correct: A thermometric property must vary continuously, measurably, and reproducibly with temperature, ideally in a linear way so the thermometer can be calibrated with uniform divisions. B is wrong because only changing at fixed temperatures would make a useless thermometer, unable to read intermediate temperatures. C is wrong because chemical properties are typically irreversible and unsuitable for repeated temperature measurement. D is wrong because a constant property cannot be used to measure temperature change at all.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Two fixed points used to calibrate a thermometer are
options: Boiling point of water and body temperature
Ice point (0°C) and steam point (100°C) at standard pressure
Room temperature and boiling point of oil
records.explanation: Correct: The two standard fixed points for calibration on the Celsius scale are the lower fixed point (0°C, melting ice at standard pressure) and upper fixed point (100°C, boiling water at standard pressure). A is wrong because body temperature is not a standard, internationally agreed fixed point. C is wrong because although absolute zero is a fixed point on the Kelvin scale, body temperature is not standard for calibration. D is wrong because room temperature and oil's boiling point are not internationally agreed fixed points.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A clinical thermometer has a constriction above the bulb. This is to
options: Prevent the mercury from returning to the bulb after removal from patient
Increase the sensitivity of the thermometer
Allow the thermometer to measure below 35°C
records.explanation: Correct: The constriction (kink) prevents mercury from flowing back into the bulb once the thermometer is removed from the patient's body, allowing the reading to be taken at leisure. B is wrong because sensitivity is determined by the bulb size and bore width, not the constriction. C is wrong because a clinical thermometer is specifically designed for the body temperature range (35–42°C) — the constriction doesn't extend this range. D is wrong because the constriction has nothing to do with preventing breakage.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A steel rod is 2 m long at 20°C. Its linear expansivity is 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹. The increase in length when heated to 120°C is
records.explanation: Correct: ΔL = αL₀ΔT = 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ × 2 × (120 − 20) = 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ × 2 × 100 = 2.4 × 10⁻³ m. B is wrong because it uses ΔT = 10 instead of the correct 100. C is wrong because it misplaces a power of 10. D is wrong because it uses only α without properly incorporating L₀ and ΔT.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The relationship between linear expansivity (α), area expansivity (β) and volume expansivity (γ) is
records.explanation: Correct: For isotropic materials, β ≈ 2α (area expansivity is twice linear expansivity) and γ ≈ 3α (volume expansivity is three times linear expansivity), approximations that hold for small expansions. A is wrong because it reverses the correct relationships. C is wrong because it swaps the correct values for β and γ. D is wrong because it inverts the relationship entirely.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Expansion joints are provided in railway lines because
options: They make the tracks look better
Thermal expansion in hot weather would cause buckling without room to expand
They reduce the weight of the track
records.explanation: Correct: Steel tracks expand as temperature rises; without expansion gaps, the expanding steel has nowhere to go and buckles, causing dangerous deformations, so the gaps provide space for thermal expansion. A is wrong because aesthetics are irrelevant to this engineering safety consideration. C is wrong because expansion joints don't affect the overall weight of the track. D is wrong because vibration absorption is handled by ballast and sleepers, not expansion joints.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Water has anomalous expansion because
options: It contracts on heating from 0°C to 4°C, reaching maximum density at 4°C
It expands on cooling from 4°C to 0°C, unlike most liquids
Both A and B are aspects of water's anomalous behavior
It becomes ice at 0°C and ice is less dense than water
records.explanation: Correct: Water's anomalous expansion means it contracts and increases in density from 0°C to 4°C (reaching maximum density at 4°C), then expands normally above that; it also expands on cooling below 4°C, due to hydrogen bonding and the crystal structure of ice. A is only partially correct as an answer because the cooling behavior below 4°C is also anomalous. B is only partially correct as an answer because the heating behavior above 4°C is also part of the anomaly. D is wrong because ice being less dense than water is a RESULT of anomalous expansion, not an explanation of it.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The real expansivity of a liquid is related to apparent expansivity by
options: Real = Apparent + Expansivity of container material
records.explanation: Correct: Apparent expansivity is what's observed, i.e. expansion of liquid minus expansion of container, so Real expansivity = Apparent expansivity + Cubic expansivity of the container glass. B is wrong because this would give a value less than the apparent expansivity, which is incorrect. C and D are wrong because multiplication or division have no physical basis in this relationship.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A gas at 27°C has a volume of 5 L at a pressure of 2 atm. What is its volume at 127°C and 4 atm?
records.explanation: Correct: Using PV/T = constant: T₁ = 300 K, T₂ = 400 K. V₂ = P₁V₁T₂/(T₁P₂) = (2 × 5 × 400)/(300 × 4) = 4000/1200 = 3.33 L. B is wrong because 2.5 L results from not converting temperatures to Kelvin. C is wrong because 10 L ignores the doubling of pressure. D is wrong because 6.67 L misapplies the combined gas law.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Boyle's law states that for a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature
options: Pressure is directly proportional to volume
Pressure is inversely proportional to volume
Volume is directly proportional to temperature
Pressure is directly proportional to temperature
records.explanation: Correct: Boyle's law states PV = constant at constant T, so P ∝ 1/V — when volume decreases, pressure increases proportionally, as in compressed air, in an isothermal process. A is wrong because pressure is INVERSELY, not directly, proportional to volume. C is wrong because volume proportional to temperature is Charles' law, which holds at constant P, not constant T. D is wrong because pressure proportional to temperature is the pressure law, which holds at constant V.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The temperature at which a gas would theoretically have zero volume or zero pressure is called
records.explanation: Correct: Absolute zero (0 K = −273°C) is the theoretical temperature at which gas molecules have no thermal kinetic energy, so gas pressure and volume would theoretically reach zero at this point. A is wrong because critical temperature is the point above which a gas cannot be liquefied by pressure alone. C is wrong because melting point is where a solid changes to liquid. D is wrong because dew point is where water vapour begins to condense.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A van der Waals gas differs from an ideal gas because
options: Its molecules have finite size and experience intermolecular forces
Temperature has no effect on it
records.explanation: Correct: The van der Waals equation (P + a/V²)(V − b) = nRT corrects for the finite molecular volume (b) and intermolecular attractive forces (a); real gases deviate from ideal behavior especially at high pressure and low temperature. B is wrong because zero molecular size is actually an IDEAL gas assumption. C is wrong because obeying PV = nRT exactly is the definition of an ideal gas, not a van der Waals gas. D is wrong because temperature affects the behavior of all gases.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: 5 kg of water is heated from 20°C to 80°C. The heat energy absorbed is (specific heat capacity of water = 4200 Jkg⁻¹K⁻¹)
records.explanation: Correct: Q = mcΔT = 5 × 4200 × (80 − 20) = 5 × 4200 × 60 = 1,260,000 J = 1.26 MJ. B is wrong because it uses m = 0.5 kg instead of the correct 5 kg. C is wrong because it calculates for ΔT = 20°C, only part of the actual temperature range. D is wrong because it incorrectly uses ΔT = 12°C.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The specific latent heat of fusion of ice is 336,000 Jkg⁻¹. The heat required to melt 500 g of ice at 0°C is
records.explanation: Correct: Q = mLf = 0.5 × 336,000 = 168,000 J, noting that 500 g must be converted to 0.5 kg. B is wrong because it uses m = 0.05 kg, an incorrect unit conversion. C is wrong because 672,000 J = 2 × mLf doubles the mass erroneously. D is wrong because 336,000 J = Lf × 1 kg simply ignores the actual mass given.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Boiling differs from evaporation in that boiling
options: Occurs only at the surface of a liquid
Occurs throughout the liquid at a fixed temperature and produces bubbles
records.explanation: Correct: Boiling occurs throughout the bulk of the liquid at a specific temperature (the boiling point), forming bubbles, whereas evaporation occurs only at the surface at any temperature below boiling point. A is wrong because a surface-only process describes evaporation, not boiling. C is wrong because occurring at any temperature is a feature of evaporation, not boiling. D is wrong because boiling requires the same latent heat as evaporation at the same temperature — it doesn't require less energy.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Increasing pressure on the surface of a boiling liquid will
options: Have no effect on boiling point
records.explanation: Correct: Higher external pressure requires the vapour pressure to reach a higher value before boiling begins, meaning more heat is needed, so the boiling point rises — this is the principle behind pressure cookers. A is wrong because it's DECREASING pressure that lowers the boiling point, not increasing it. C is wrong because pressure significantly affects the boiling point. D is wrong because increasing pressure on a liquid causes it to boil at a higher temperature, not solidify.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A pressure cooker raises the boiling point of water above 100°C. This means that food cooks faster because
options: The water contains more pressure energy
The higher temperature increases the rate of chemical reactions in cooking
records.explanation: Correct: At higher temperatures, such as 120°C in a pressure cooker, cooking reactions proceed faster, since the rate of most chemical reactions approximately doubles for every 10°C rise (per the Arrhenius principle). A is wrong because pressure energy doesn't directly cook food — temperature is the key factor. C is wrong because the dryness of steam is irrelevant to cooking speed. D is wrong because the amount of water used isn't the key factor in cooking speed.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Relative humidity is defined as the ratio of
options: Actual mass of water vapor in air to mass of water vapor needed to saturate the same air at the same temperature
Temperature of air to dew point temperature
Pressure of water vapor to atmospheric pressure
Volume of water vapor to volume of dry air
records.explanation: Correct: Relative humidity (RH) = (mass of water vapour in the sample / mass needed to saturate at the same temperature) × 100%, equivalently expressed as the ratio of saturated vapour pressure at dew point to that at air temperature. B is wrong because a temperature ratio is not the definition of RH. C is wrong because the ratio of water vapour pressure to atmospheric pressure relates to absolute humidity, not the RH definition. D is wrong because a volume ratio is not the standard definition of relative humidity.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The dew point is the temperature at which
options: All water vapor condenses into rain
The water vapor in air becomes saturated (SVP equals actual vapor pressure)
records.explanation: Correct: The dew point is the temperature at which air becomes saturated with its existing amount of water vapour (RH = 100%); at this point, condensation begins and dew forms on cool surfaces. A is wrong because not all vapour condenses at the dew point — only the excess above saturation does. C is wrong because ice (frost) forms below 0°C specifically when the dew point is below 0°C, but that's not the general definition. D is wrong because at the dew point, humidity is actually 100%, not 0%.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A wet and dry bulb hygrometer shows wet bulb temperature of 18°C and dry bulb temperature of 24°C. The difference indicates
options: Evaporation is occurring from the wet bulb, indicating unsaturated air with RH < 100%
records.explanation: Correct: When wet and dry bulb temperatures differ, evaporation is cooling the wet bulb; a greater difference means drier air and a lower relative humidity (equal readings would mean 100% RH, i.e. saturated air with no evaporation). A is wrong because a temperature rise isn't inferred from the difference alone. C is wrong because saturated air (100% RH) would show equal wet and dry bulb temperatures, not a difference. D is wrong because rain cannot be inferred from a hygrometer reading.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Brownian motion provides evidence for
options: The continuous and random motion of molecules in a fluid
The existence of atoms only in solids
records.explanation: Correct: Brownian motion, the random movement of pollen grains in water observed by Robert Brown, shows that liquid molecules are in continuous, random motion, continually bombarding and jostling suspended particles. A is wrong because Brownian motion is a particle phenomenon — wave-particle duality is a separate concept (de Broglie's hypothesis). C is wrong because molecular motion occurs in all states of matter — solids, liquids, and gases. D is wrong because Brownian motion actually occurs due to molecular bombardment, meaning intermolecular forces do exist.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Surface tension is explained by molecular theory as arising from
options: Cohesion between molecules at the surface and net inward molecular force due to unbalanced cohesive forces
Adhesion of water to air molecules
The low density of surface molecules
records.explanation: Correct: Surface molecules experience cohesive forces from below and the sides but not from above (since there's no liquid above them), creating a net inward force that produces surface tension — the 'skin' effect that lets insects walk on water. A is wrong because gravity causes liquids to flow, not surface tension. C is wrong because water-air adhesion is very weak compared to water-water cohesion. D is wrong because density is uniform at the surface — surface tension is a force effect, not a density effect.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Diffusion occurs more rapidly in gases than in liquids because
options: Gas molecules have larger intermolecular distances and higher average speeds
Liquids are more viscous than solids
Gas molecules have stronger intermolecular forces
records.explanation: Correct: In gases, molecules are widely spaced with a large mean free path and move at high speeds (hundreds of m/s), whereas in liquids, molecules are closely packed with stronger intermolecular forces that slow diffusion significantly. A is wrong because gas molecules are often lighter than liquid molecules, e.g. air vs water, which opposes this claim. C is wrong because comparing liquids to solids' viscosity is irrelevant to a gas-liquid comparison. D is wrong because gas molecules actually have WEAKER intermolecular forces, which is why they diffuse faster.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Capillarity (capillary action) occurs because of
options: The interplay between adhesion (liquid to tube) and cohesion (liquid to liquid) forces
Atmospheric pressure pushing liquid up the tube
The weight of liquid in the tube
records.explanation: Correct: Capillary action depends on whether adhesion (liquid-tube) or cohesion (liquid-liquid) is stronger; if adhesion exceeds cohesion (as with water in glass), the liquid rises with a concave meniscus, while if cohesion exceeds adhesion (as with mercury in glass), the liquid is depressed with a convex meniscus. A is wrong because cohesion alone would cause the liquid to fall, not rise. C is wrong because atmospheric pressure acts on both the inside and outside of the tube — it doesn't directly cause capillarity. D is wrong because the weight of the liquid actually works against capillary rise, not for it.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: In a vacuum flask (thermos flask), heat loss by radiation is minimized by
options: The silvered inner surfaces which reflect radiated heat
records.explanation: Correct: The silvered inner surfaces of the vacuum flask reflect radiation back, minimizing heat transfer by radiation, while the vacuum between the walls separately prevents conduction and convection. A is wrong because the double walls create the vacuum gap, which is what stops conduction/convection — silvering is what stops radiation specifically. C is wrong because the stopper reduces convection from the opening but isn't the primary control for radiation. D is wrong because the outer casing provides only physical protection.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Heat transfer by convection requires
options: A medium and bulk movement of the fluid carrying thermal energy
records.explanation: Correct: Convection involves the bulk movement of a fluid (liquid or gas) carrying thermal energy; hot fluid rises since it's less dense and cool fluid sinks since it's denser, creating convection currents, which requires a medium, not a vacuum. A is wrong because convection cannot occur in a vacuum — it requires a fluid medium. C is wrong because contact between solid surfaces describes conduction, not convection. D is wrong because electromagnetic radiation describes a separate heat transfer mechanism (radiation), not convection.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A good absorber of heat radiation is also a good
records.explanation: Correct: By Kirchhoff's law of radiation, good absorbers are also good emitters at the same temperature; a perfect absorber (black body) is also the best emitter, and black surfaces absorb and emit more radiation than polished surfaces. A is wrong because good absorbers are actually POOR reflectors — they're opposites. C and D are wrong because conduction and emission are different heat transfer mechanisms — absorption relates specifically to radiation, not necessarily to conduction.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Land breeze occurs at night because
options: The sea heats up faster than land and the warm air rises over the sea
The land cools down faster than sea at night, so warm air rises over sea and cool air from land moves to replace it
The land is always warmer than the sea
Wind always blows from sea to land
records.explanation: Correct: At night, land cools faster than sea since the sea retains heat longer; warm air rises over the warmer sea, and cooler air from land blows seaward to replace it, forming the land breeze (land to sea). A is wrong because this actually describes the sea breeze, which occurs during the daytime when land heats up faster. C is wrong because land is warmer during the day but cooler at night — it isn't always warmer. D is wrong because wind from sea to land describes the SEA BREEZE (daytime), not the land breeze.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The rate of heat conduction through a material is increased by
options: Increasing the thickness of the material
Increasing the cross-sectional area and temperature gradient
Using a material with low thermal conductivity
records.explanation: Correct: Rate of heat flow Q/t = kA(ΔT/L), where k is thermal conductivity, A is cross-sectional area, ΔT is temperature difference, and L is thickness; increasing A and ΔT increases the heat flow rate. A is wrong because decreasing the temperature gradient (ΔT/L) actually DECREASES the heat flow rate. B is wrong because increasing thickness L DECREASES the heat flow rate. D is wrong because low thermal conductivity k DECREASES the heat flow rate.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The frequency of a wave is 500 Hz and its wavelength is 0.4 m. The velocity of the wave is
records.explanation: Correct: v = fλ = 500 × 0.4 = 200 ms⁻¹, using the standard wave equation relating velocity, frequency, and wavelength. B is wrong because 1250 ms⁻¹ = f/λ divides instead of multiplying. C is wrong because 0.0008 = λ/f inverts the formula. D is wrong because 2000 ms⁻¹ results from an arithmetic error.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Polarization of waves is only possible for
records.explanation: Correct: Polarization restricts vibration to one plane, which is only possible when vibrations are perpendicular to propagation, i.e. for transverse waves; longitudinal waves like sound vibrate along the propagation direction and cannot be polarized. A is wrong because longitudinal waves CANNOT be polarized, since their vibration is along the propagation direction. B is wrong because sound is a longitudinal wave and therefore cannot be polarized. D is wrong because not all waves can be polarized — only transverse waves can.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Beat frequency is produced when two sound waves of frequencies 440 Hz and 444 Hz are sounded together. The beat frequency is
records.explanation: Correct: Beat frequency = |f₁ − f₂| = |440 − 444| = 4 Hz, the rate at which constructive interference alternates, heard as 4 pulses of loudness per second. A is wrong because 884 Hz = f₁ + f₂ gives the sum, a different quantity from beats. C is wrong because 440 Hz is just one of the two original frequencies. D is wrong because 2 Hz halves the correct result without any valid basis.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Sound travels faster in
records.explanation: Correct: The speed of sound increases with the elasticity and density of the medium, following the order solids > liquids > gases; in steel it's roughly 5000 ms⁻¹, versus about 1500 ms⁻¹ in water and 340 ms⁻¹ in air. A is wrong because sound cannot travel in a vacuum at all — it requires a material medium. B is wrong because air, a low-density gas, is actually the slowest medium for sound among the options given. C is wrong because water, while faster than air, is still slower than steel.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: An echo is heard 2 seconds after a sound is produced. If the speed of sound in air is 340 ms⁻¹, the distance to the reflecting surface is
records.explanation: Correct: Total distance = speed × time = 340 × 2 = 680 m, which is the round-trip distance to the wall and back, so the distance to the wall = 680/2 = 340 m. B is wrong because 680 m is the total round-trip distance, not the distance to the wall alone. C is wrong because 170 m = 340/2 mistakenly uses only 1 second instead of the full round-trip calculation. D is wrong because 85 m = 340/4 has no valid basis.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The pitch of a musical note is determined by its
records.explanation: Correct: Pitch is the perceptual attribute of sound related to frequency — higher frequency means higher pitch, while amplitude determines loudness (and intensity), and waveform determines quality (timbre). A is wrong because amplitude determines loudness/intensity, not pitch. B is wrong because intensity determines loudness (measured in decibels), not pitch. D is wrong because waveform (the shape of the wave) determines the quality or timbre of a sound, not its pitch.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A closed pipe of length 0.5 m resonates in its fundamental mode. The frequency of the note produced is (speed of sound = 340 ms⁻¹)
records.explanation: Correct: For a closed pipe (one open end, one closed end), fundamental frequency f = v/(4L) = 340/(4 × 0.5) = 340/2 = 170 Hz, since L = λ/4 for such a pipe. B is wrong because 340 Hz uses f = v/(2L), the formula for an OPEN pipe instead. C is wrong because 680 Hz = v/L skips the factor of 4 entirely. D is wrong because 85 Hz = v/(8L) uses the wrong harmonic.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Reverberation differs from echo in that
options: Reverberation is heard as a distinct separate sound
Reverberation is the persistence of sound due to multiple reflections in an enclosed space
Echo is caused by multiple reflections
records.explanation: Correct: Reverberation involves multiple rapid reflections that blend together, prolonging the original sound (heard in halls and rooms), while echo is a distinct separate reflection heard after a time delay, requiring sufficient distance to the reflecting surface. A is wrong because a distinct separate sound describes an ECHO, not reverberation. C is wrong because multiple reflections in an enclosed space cause reverberation, whereas echoes can arise from a single reflection. D is wrong because reverberation occurs in enclosed indoor spaces, not outdoors.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The fundamental frequency of a vibrating string is increased by
options: Increasing the length of the string
Decreasing the tension in the string
Increasing the tension or decreasing the length or using a lighter string
Increasing the mass per unit length
records.explanation: Correct: The fundamental frequency of a string is f = (1/2L)√(T/μ), so frequency increases with higher tension T, shorter length L, or lower mass per unit length μ (a lighter string). A is wrong because increasing length actually DECREASES frequency, since f ∝ 1/L. B is wrong because decreasing tension DECREASES frequency, since f ∝ √T. D is wrong because increasing the mass per unit length μ DECREASES frequency, since f ∝ 1/√μ.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The image formed by a pinhole camera is
options: Real, inverted, and diminished or magnified depending on distances
records.explanation: Correct: A pinhole camera forms a real, inverted image, with the size depending on the ratio of image distance to object distance — if image distance exceeds object distance, the image is magnified. A is wrong because virtual and upright images are characteristic of plane mirror images, not pinhole cameras. C is wrong because the image formed by a pinhole camera is real (it forms on a screen), not virtual. D is wrong because a real image from a pinhole camera is always inverted, never upright.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A concave mirror has a focal length of 15 cm. An object is placed 10 cm in front of it. The image is
options: Real, inverted, at 30 cm behind the mirror
Virtual, upright, 30 cm behind the mirror
records.explanation: Correct: Using 1/f = 1/v + 1/u with f = −15 cm and u = −10 cm: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = −1/15 + 1/10 = 1/30, so v = +30 cm, meaning the image is behind the mirror (virtual); since the object is inside the focal length, the image is virtual, upright, and magnified. A is wrong because real, inverted images form only when the object is beyond the focal point — here the object at 10 cm is inside f = 15 cm. C is wrong because the image is at infinity only when the object is exactly at the focal point. D is wrong because a real image would require v to be negative, in front of the mirror.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The laws of reflection state that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, and both angles are measured
options: From the normal to the surface at the point of incidence
records.explanation: Correct: Both the angle of incidence and angle of reflection are measured from the NORMAL (perpendicular) to the surface at the point of incidence, not from the surface itself. A is wrong because angles measured from the surface would be the complement (90° − θ) of the correct angles. C is wrong because the horizontal is irrelevant, since the normal's direction depends on the surface's orientation. D is wrong because the angles are measured from the normal, not from each other directly.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A convex mirror always forms images that are
options: Virtual, upright, and diminished regardless of object position
records.explanation: Correct: A convex (diverging) mirror always forms virtual, upright, and diminished images for all real object positions, which is why it gives a wide field of view and is used as a rear-view mirror. A is wrong because real, inverted images are formed by concave mirrors when the object is beyond the focus, not by convex mirrors. C is wrong because real upright images don't form with any mirror — real images from mirrors are always inverted. D is wrong because virtual images from convex mirrors are always upright and smaller, never inverted.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: When light passes from air into glass, it bends toward the normal because
options: Light slows down in glass (denser medium) and the wavefront is refracted
records.explanation: Correct: When light enters a denser medium like glass, it slows down; the part of the wavefront entering the glass first slows first, causing the wave to bend toward the normal (refractive index n = c/v_medium > 1 for glass). A is wrong because light actually SLOWS DOWN, rather than speeding up, in a denser medium. C is wrong because wavelength DECREASES, not increases, in a denser medium since λ = v/f and v decreases. D is wrong because frequency remains constant as light crosses a boundary — it's wavelength and speed that change.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The critical angle for glass-air interface is related to refractive index n by
records.explanation: Correct: At the critical angle C, the refracted ray travels exactly along the glass-air boundary (90°); using Snell's law, n sin C = 1 × sin 90° = 1, so sin C = 1/n. A is wrong because sin C = n would give C > 90° for n > 1, which is physically impossible. C is wrong because a cosine relation has no derivation from Snell's law in this context. D is wrong because a tangent relation has no basis in the refraction equations.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A converging lens has a focal length of 20 cm. An object is placed 30 cm from the lens. The image distance is
options: 60 cm on the same side as the object
60 cm on the opposite side from the object
records.explanation: Correct: Using 1/f = 1/v + 1/u with sign convention (u = −30, f = +20): 1/v = 1/20 − 1/30 = 3/60 − 2/60 = 1/60, giving v = +60 cm, meaning the image forms on the opposite side of the lens from the object (a real image). A is wrong because being on the same side as the object would indicate a virtual image, but v = +60 places the image on the opposite side (real). C is wrong because 12 cm = (20×30)/(20+30) uses the wrong formula. D is wrong because 120 cm results from an arithmetic error.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Dispersion of white light by a prism occurs because
options: The prism is denser than air
Different colors (wavelengths) have different refractive indices in glass, causing different degrees of bending
White light contains only red and violet components
The prism reflects different colors at different angles
records.explanation: Correct: In dispersion, violet light has a higher refractive index in glass than red light, so it bends more; white light thus separates into a full spectrum (ROYGBIV), a phenomenon known as chromatic dispersion. A is wrong because while the prism being denser causes overall refraction, dispersion specifically requires different refractive indices for different wavelengths. C is wrong because white light actually contains all visible colors (ROYGBIV), not just red and violet. D is wrong because it's refraction, not reflection, that separates the colors in a prism.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The primary colors of light are
records.explanation: Correct: The primary colors of LIGHT, based on additive mixing, are Red, Green, and Blue (RGB); mixing all three gives white light, distinct from the primary pigment colors used in art. A is wrong because red, yellow, and blue are primary PIGMENT colors used in subtractive mixing, not light primaries. C is wrong because orange and violet are secondary/tertiary colors within the visible spectrum, not primaries. D is wrong because yellow, cyan, and magenta are actually the primary colors used in printing/subtractive mixing.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The electromagnetic wave with the shortest wavelength is
records.explanation: Correct: In the electromagnetic spectrum, wavelength increases (and frequency decreases) in the order: Gamma rays < X-rays < UV < Visible < IR < Microwaves < Radio waves, so gamma rays have the shortest wavelength and highest energy. A is wrong because radio waves actually have the LONGEST wavelength, the opposite of what's asked. B is wrong because visible light sits in the middle of the EM spectrum. C is wrong because X-rays, while shorter than visible light, are still longer than gamma rays.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The refractive index of glass is 1.5. The speed of light in glass is (c = 3 × 10⁸ ms⁻¹)
records.explanation: Correct: n = c/v_glass, so v_glass = c/n = (3 × 10⁸)/1.5 = 2.0 × 10⁸ ms⁻¹. A is wrong because 4.5 × 10⁸ = n × c multiplies instead of dividing. C is wrong because 1.5 × 10⁸ = c/2n incorrectly divides by 2n. D is wrong because 3.0 × 10⁸ is simply the speed in vacuum, not in glass.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The power of a lens is +4 D (dioptres). Its focal length is
records.explanation: Correct: Power P = 1/f (in metres), so f = 1/P = 1/4 = 0.25 m = 25 cm; the positive power indicates a converging (convex) lens. A is wrong because 4 m confuses f = P instead of the correct relation f = 1/P. B is wrong because 0.4 m = 1/2.5, not 1/4. D is wrong because 25 m = 1/0.04 likely results from a unit confusion.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The image formed by a concave lens is always
options: Real, inverted, and between F and 2F
Virtual, upright, and diminished for real objects
records.explanation: Correct: A concave (diverging) lens ALWAYS forms virtual, upright, and diminished images for real objects, regardless of the object's position, similar in behavior to a convex mirror. A is wrong because real, inverted images between F and 2F are formed by convex (converging) lenses, not concave ones. C is wrong because magnified real images beyond 2F require a converging lens with the object inside F. D is wrong because virtual images from a concave lens are always smaller, never magnified.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Optical fibers work on the principle of
records.explanation: Correct: Optical fibers carry light signals over long distances via total internal reflection; light hits the fiber wall at an angle greater than the critical angle and is repeatedly reflected back into the fiber. A is wrong because regular reflection occurs at polished flat surfaces, which isn't applicable to how fibers guide light. C is wrong because diffraction would cause light to spread out and escape the fiber, defeating its purpose. D is wrong because polarization is a property of transverse waves, not the mechanism by which fiber optics function.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: In a simple astronomical telescope in normal adjustment, the final image is formed
options: At the near point of the eye
Between F and 2F of the eyepiece
records.explanation: Correct: In normal adjustment, a telescope is set so the final image forms at infinity, with parallel rays entering the eye, giving the least eye strain for prolonged observation. A is wrong because an image at the near point corresponds to a telescope adjusted for near-point viewing, which gives maximum magnification but causes eye strain. C is wrong because an image between F and 2F applies to an object position for a magnifying glass, not a telescope in normal adjustment. D is wrong because the objective lens forms only the intermediate image, not the final image seen by the eye.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A rainbow is formed by
options: Refraction and internal reflection of sunlight in raindrops with dispersion of colors
Diffraction of sunlight through water droplets
records.explanation: Correct: A rainbow forms when sunlight enters a raindrop, is refracted (dispersed), internally reflected at the back of the drop, and refracted again on exit, with different colors emerging at different angles due to their different refractive indices. A is wrong because reflection from clouds actually produces halos or coronas, not rainbows. C is wrong because diffraction produces different patterns, like iridescence, and isn't the primary mechanism for rainbows. D is wrong because polarization is only a secondary effect of rainbow light — it's not the formation mechanism.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Two point charges of +3 μC and +12 μC are separated by 0.3 m. The force between them is (k = 9 × 10⁹ Nm²C⁻²)
records.explanation: Correct: F = kq₁q₂/r² = (9 × 10⁹ × 3 × 10⁻⁶ × 12 × 10⁻⁶)/(0.3)² = (9 × 10⁹ × 36 × 10⁻¹²)/0.09 = 3.6 N. B is wrong because 36 N contains an arithmetic error, likely from using r = 0.1 m instead of 0.3 m. C is wrong because 0.36 N is off by a factor of 10. D is wrong because 360 N is off by a factor of 100.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The electric field lines between two oppositely charged parallel plates are
options: Curved and pointing from negative to positive plate
Uniform, parallel, and pointing from positive to negative plate
Curved, pointing from positive to negative only near the edges
records.explanation: Correct: Between infinite parallel plates with opposite charges, the electric field is uniform in both magnitude and direction, with field lines running parallel and straight, pointing from the positive plate to the negative plate. A is wrong because field lines point FROM positive TO negative, i.e. in the direction of force on a positive test charge, not the reverse. C is wrong because a radial field exists around isolated point charges, not between parallel plates. D is wrong because the field is uniform in the middle region — only near the edges does it become non-uniform due to fringing effects.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A charge of 2 μC is placed at a point where the electric field intensity is 5 × 10⁴ NC⁻¹. The force on the charge is
records.explanation: Correct: F = qE = 2 × 10⁻⁶ × 5 × 10⁴ = 10 × 10⁻² = 0.1 N. B is wrong because 2.5 × 10¹⁰ = E/q inverts the correct formula. C is wrong because 1.0 N results from an arithmetic error. D is wrong because 0.01 N includes an extra unwarranted factor of 10⁻¹.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Lightning conductors protect buildings from lightning by
options: Slowly discharging the electric field between cloud and ground via a conducting path, preventing a sudden discharge
Reflecting lightning away from the building
Insulating the building from the ground
records.explanation: Correct: A lightning conductor, a pointed spike on the roof connected to earth, continuously leaks charge between cloud and earth, reducing the potential difference; if lightning does strike, the conductor provides a low-resistance path to earth, protecting the building. A is wrong because lightning conductors cannot prevent charge from forming in clouds. C is wrong because lightning conductors do not reflect lightning — they conduct the charge safely to earth. D is wrong because lightning conductors must be CONNECTED to earth, providing a conducting path rather than insulation.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The gold-leaf electroscope detects charge by
options: The attraction between the gold leaf and the metal rod
The divergence of the gold leaf from the metal plate due to like charges repelling each other
The current flowing through the gold leaf
records.explanation: Correct: When charge is applied to the electroscope, it spreads to the metal plate and gold leaf; since both now carry like charges, they repel each other and the gold leaf diverges from the plate, with greater charge producing greater divergence. A is wrong because like charges on the leaf and plate repel, they don't attract. C is wrong because a gold-leaf electroscope measures static charge, not a flowing current. D is wrong because electrostatic charge detection has nothing to do with magnetism.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The electric potential at a point is defined as
options: The force per unit positive charge at that point
The work done per unit positive charge in bringing a small positive test charge from infinity to that point
The electric field intensity at that point
records.explanation: Correct: Electric potential V = W/q, the work done per unit positive charge in bringing a small positive test charge from infinity to that point (V = kQ/r for a point charge), measured in volts. A is wrong because force per unit charge is actually electric field intensity (E), not potential. C is wrong because electric field E is force per charge (units of V/m), which is not the same quantity as potential (V). D is wrong because charge per unit area is instead the surface charge density (σ).

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The energy stored in a capacitor of capacitance C charged to voltage V is
records.explanation: Correct: Energy stored E = ½CV² = ½QV = Q²/2C, representing the energy stored in the electric field between the plates. A is wrong because CV equals the charge Q, not the energy. C is wrong because C²V has the wrong dimensions to represent energy. D is wrong because 2CV² simply doubles the correct formula.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor is INCREASED by
options: Increasing the distance between the plates
Decreasing the area of the plates
Inserting a dielectric material between the plates
records.explanation: Correct: C = εA/d = ε₀εᵣA/d, so capacitance increases when the dielectric constant εᵣ increases (by inserting a dielectric), when area A increases, or when plate separation d decreases. A is wrong because increasing distance d actually DECREASES capacitance, since C ∝ 1/d. B is wrong because decreasing area DECREASES capacitance, since C ∝ A. D is wrong because voltage does not affect capacitance at all — C = Q/V, with V and Q changing proportionally to keep C constant.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Capacitors are used in tuning circuits of radios because
options: They store energy for the radio
Variable capacitors can change the resonant frequency to select different stations
records.explanation: Correct: In an LC tuning circuit, the resonant frequency f = 1/(2π√LC), so changing the capacitance using a variable capacitor changes the resonant frequency, allowing selection of different radio stations. A is wrong because while capacitors can store energy, this isn't their primary function in a tuning circuit. C is wrong because blocking DC is a general function of capacitors, but it's not why they're used specifically in tuning circuits. D is wrong because it's transistors, not capacitors, that amplify signals.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Two capacitors of 3 μF and 6 μF are connected in series. The equivalent capacitance is
records.explanation: Correct: For capacitors in series, 1/C = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ = 1/3 + 1/6 = 2/6 + 1/6 = 3/6 = 1/2, so C = 2 μF. A is wrong because 9 μF = C₁ + C₂ mistakenly applies the parallel formula. C is wrong because 18 μF = C₁ × C₂ is just the product, without the sum in the denominator that the series formula requires. D is wrong because 0.5 μF = 1/(C₁ + C₂) inverts the calculation incorrectly.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The internal resistance of a cell is 0.5 Ω and its emf is 2 V. When connected to an external resistance of 1.5 Ω, the terminal voltage is
records.explanation: Correct: Current I = EMF/(R + r) = 2/(1.5 + 0.5) = 2/2 = 1 A, so terminal voltage = EMF − Ir = 2 − 1 × 0.5 = 1.5 V (equivalently V = IR = 1 × 1.5 = 1.5 V). B is wrong because 2.0 V is the emf itself, not the terminal voltage, which must account for the internal resistance drop. C is wrong because 0.5 V = Ir is the lost voltage (voltage drop across internal resistance), not the terminal voltage. D is wrong because 1.0 V results from an arithmetic error.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Ohm's law states that the current through a conductor is proportional to the potential difference across it, provided
options: The physical conditions (especially temperature) remain constant
records.explanation: Correct: Ohm's law, V = IR with R constant, holds only when the physical conditions, particularly temperature, remain unchanged, since temperature changes alter resistance, making the law invalid for non-ohmic conductors. A is wrong because semiconductors actually do not strictly obey Ohm's law — they are non-ohmic. C is wrong because Ohm's law applies to both AC and DC for ohmic conductors, not specifically to alternating current. D is wrong because Ohm's law primarily applies to metallic conductors; electrolytes may not obey it.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The resistivity of a material is defined as the resistance of
options: A sample of the material of any size
A conductor of unit length and unit cross-sectional area
A conductor 1 m long and 1 cm² cross-section
records.explanation: Correct: Resistivity ρ = RA/L is the resistance of a conductor with unit length (1 m) and unit cross-sectional area (1 m²); it is a material property, independent of the sample's actual size, with units of Ω·m. A is wrong because resistivity is size-independent — it's specifically a material property, not tied to 'any size.' C is wrong because the standard SI reference uses 1 m² cross-section, not 1 cm². D is wrong because resistivity is defined at a standard reference temperature in general, but 0°C specifically is not part of the definition — temperature affects resistivity but doesn't define it.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A potentiometer is preferred over a voltmeter for measuring EMF because
options: It is cheaper and easier to use
It draws no current from the cell when balanced, so it measures true EMF
It has a lower resistance than a voltmeter
records.explanation: Correct: At the balance point of a potentiometer, no current flows from the cell being tested, so there's no internal resistance drop (Ir = 0), meaning terminal voltage equals the true EMF; a voltmeter, by contrast, draws current and causes a voltage drop, giving a reading less than the true EMF. A is wrong because cost and ease of use are not the technical advantage being described. C is wrong because a potentiometer effectively has INFINITE resistance at balance, the opposite of having a lower resistance. D is wrong because potentiometers work with both AC and DC, though they are primarily used with DC.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The meter bridge (Wheatstone bridge) is used to measure
options: Unknown resistance by comparing with a known resistance at balance
records.explanation: Correct: At balance, P/Q = R/S (where S is the unknown resistance); the meter bridge is a practical form of Wheatstone bridge that uses a resistance wire to find the balance point where the galvanometer reads zero, allowing calculation of the unknown resistance. A is wrong because EMF is measured with a potentiometer, not a meter bridge. C is wrong because capacitance is measured with an LCR meter or an AC bridge. D is wrong because frequency measurement requires an oscilloscope or a frequency counter.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A heater rated 500 W operates at 250 V. The current drawn and resistance are
records.explanation: Correct: P = IV, so I = P/V = 500/250 = 2 A, and R = V/I = 250/2 = 125 Ω (equivalently R = V²/P = 250²/500 = 125 Ω). B is wrong because 0.5 A = V/P inverts the correct formula. C is wrong because 5 A = P/50V uses an incorrect voltage value. D is wrong because R = 250 Ω confuses the voltage value with the resistance itself.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The domestic wiring system uses parallel connection because
options: All appliances receive the same full voltage and can be independently controlled
The current is the same through all appliances
records.explanation: Correct: In parallel wiring, all devices receive the same supply voltage, each device can be switched on or off independently, and if one fails, the others continue working — series wiring would instead reduce voltage for each device. A is wrong because parallel wiring actually uses more wire, making it more expensive, not cheaper. C is wrong because having the same current through all components is a property of SERIES circuits, not parallel ones. D is wrong because parallel circuits have LOWER effective resistance than series circuits, not higher.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The fuse in an electrical circuit is designed to
options: Melt and break the circuit when current exceeds a safe limit, protecting the circuit
Measure the current in the circuit
records.explanation: Correct: A fuse is a thin wire with a low melting point; when current exceeds the rated value, the fuse heats up and melts, breaking the circuit and preventing damage to appliances or fire hazards. A is wrong because fuses limit, rather than increase, current flow. C is wrong because ammeters measure current, whereas fuses serve to protect circuits. D is wrong because capacitors store electrical energy — fuses are strictly protective devices.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Lenz's law states that the induced current in a circuit is in a direction that
options: Opposes the change in flux that causes it
Amplifies the motion causing the induction
Is perpendicular to the magnetic flux
records.explanation: Correct: Lenz's law is a statement of energy conservation in electromagnetism — the induced current opposes the change that causes it; if flux increases, the induced current creates a field opposing that increase, which is why induction requires work. B is wrong because the direction of induced current is not always clockwise — it depends on the specific geometry of the flux change. C is wrong because amplifying the motion would violate conservation of energy — Lenz's law specifically ensures opposition. D is wrong because induced current flows in a circuit loop, and describing it as perpendicular to flux misrepresents the law.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction states that the induced EMF is
options: Proportional to the current in the circuit
Equal to the rate of change of magnetic flux linkage through the circuit
Inversely proportional to the resistance of the circuit
Equal to the magnetic flux density
records.explanation: Correct: Faraday's law states EMF = −dΦ/dt = −N dΦ/dt for N turns, meaning the induced EMF equals the rate of change of magnetic flux linkage, with the negative sign representing Lenz's law. A is wrong because induced EMF depends on the rate of flux change, not on the current itself. C is wrong because resistance affects the current that flows once EMF is induced (I = EMF/R), but not the induced EMF itself. D is wrong because EMF is proportional to the RATE OF CHANGE of flux, not simply the flux density.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: An AC generator works on the principle of
options: Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction as the coil rotates in a magnetic field
records.explanation: Correct: An AC generator works by rotating a coil in a magnetic field, and the changing flux through the coil induces an alternating EMF according to Faraday's law, with the rotating coil producing a sinusoidal output. A is wrong because Lenz's law describes only the direction of the induced current, which is one aspect of generation, not the full principle. C is wrong because the motor effect is the reverse process — converting electrical current in a field into mechanical force, rather than generation. D is wrong because electrostatic induction is a static charge phenomenon, unrelated to electromagnetic generation.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A transformer has 200 primary turns and 1000 secondary turns. If the primary voltage is 240 V, the secondary voltage is
records.explanation: Correct: V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p, so V_s = V_p × (N_s/N_p) = 240 × (1000/200) = 240 × 5 = 1200 V, indicating this is a step-up transformer since N_s > N_p. A is wrong because 48 V = 240/5 mistakenly applies the step-DOWN ratio instead of step-up. C is wrong because 240 V would only apply if the turns were equal, which they aren't here. D is wrong because 2400 V = 240 × 10 uses an incorrect turns ratio of 10 instead of the correct 5.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The angle of declination at a location is the angle between
options: The horizontal and the direction of Earth's magnetic field
True (geographic) north and magnetic north at that location
The Earth's magnetic poles and geographic poles
Magnetic field lines and the vertical
records.explanation: Correct: The angle of declination (magnetic variation) is the horizontal angle between true geographic north and magnetic north at a given location, which navigators must account for when using a magnetic compass. A is wrong because this instead describes the angle of dip (inclination), the vertical component of Earth's field. C is wrong because the angle between magnetic and geographic poles is a global quantity, not the location-specific declination. D is wrong because the angle between field lines and the vertical is also the angle of dip, not declination.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The angle of dip (magnetic inclination) is 90° at the
records.explanation: Correct: At the magnetic poles, Earth's magnetic field points vertically (downward or upward), giving an angle of dip of 90°; at the magnetic equator, the field is horizontal and the dip is 0°. A is wrong because at the magnetic equator, the dip is 0°, since the field is horizontal there. B is wrong because the geographic equator is close to the magnetic equator, where dip is approximately 0°. D is wrong because at the tropics, the dip has intermediate values, somewhere between 0° and 90°.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Eddy currents in transformer cores are reduced by
options: Laminating the core with insulated thin sheets of iron
records.explanation: Correct: Eddy currents are circulating currents induced within the core; laminating the core (layering thin iron sheets insulated from each other) restricts eddy currents to small loops within each sheet, greatly reducing their magnitude and the resulting heating loss. A is wrong because a solid core actually provides a large cross-section for eddy currents, the opposite of the intended solution. C is wrong because higher frequency actually induces LARGER eddy currents, since dΦ/dt increases. D is wrong because copper is a better conductor than iron, which would increase, not decrease, eddy current losses.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: In a DC motor, the function of the commutator is to
options: Increase the speed of the motor
Reverse the current in the coil every half turn to maintain continuous rotation in one direction
Supply current to the field magnets
records.explanation: Correct: The commutator (split ring) reverses the current in the armature coil every half revolution; without this, the coil would simply oscillate back and forth, but the commutator ensures the torque always acts in the same direction, maintaining continuous rotation. A is wrong because speed is controlled by voltage or current, not by the commutator's function. C is wrong because field current is supplied through separate connections, not through the commutator. D is wrong because friction is reduced by bearings, not by the commutator.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The inductance of a coil is defined as the ratio of
records.explanation: Correct: Inductance L = NΦ/I, the flux linkage per unit current (alternatively L = EMF/(dI/dt)), measured in Henry (H); an inductor opposes changes in current through electromagnetic induction. A is wrong because EMF divided by current gives resistance (per Ohm's law), not inductance. C is wrong because current divided by voltage gives conductance (1/R), a different quantity. D is wrong because power divided by current gives voltage (since P = IV), unrelated to inductance.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A moving coil galvanometer uses a radial magnetic field to ensure that
options: The coil vibrates at high frequency
The deflection is directly proportional to current at all angles (linear scale)
Temperature does not affect the reading
records.explanation: Correct: The radial field, created using curved pole pieces with a soft iron cylinder, ensures the field is always parallel to the plane of the coil at all angles, making the torque (and hence deflection) directly proportional to current, giving a linear, uniform scale. A is wrong because the frequency of vibration is not related to the radial field's design purpose. C is wrong because galvanometers detect current — they don't amplify it in any way. D is wrong because temperature compensation is achieved through materials with low temperature coefficients, not through the radial field design.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The RMS (root mean square) value of an AC current is related to its peak value I₀ by
records.explanation: Correct: For a sinusoidal AC current, I_rms = I₀/√2 ≈ 0.707 I₀, the equivalent DC value that produces the same heating effect; the mains supply voltage (220–240 V) is quoted as an RMS value. A is wrong because 2I₀ doubles the peak, giving a value larger than the peak itself, which is impossible for RMS. B is wrong because I₀/2 = 0.5I₀ is not the correct RMS ratio, which is 1/√2 ≈ 0.707. D is wrong because √2 × I₀ exceeds I₀, but RMS must always be less than or equal to the peak value.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: In a purely capacitive AC circuit, the current
options: Is in phase with the voltage
records.explanation: Correct: For a pure capacitor, I = C dV/dt, so current is proportional to the rate of change of voltage, causing the current to lead the voltage by 90° (π/2 radians) — remembered via the mnemonic 'CIVIL' (In Capacitor, I leads V; in inductor L, V leads I). A is wrong because it's the voltage, not the current, that lags in an INDUCTOR by 90° — this describes the opposite component. B is wrong because being in phase describes the behavior of a pure resistor, not a capacitor. D is wrong because a 45° phase difference occurs in RC or RL circuits, not in a pure C or L component alone.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: At resonance in an RLC series circuit
options: Impedance is maximum and current is minimum
Inductive reactance equals capacitive reactance and impedance equals resistance
The circuit behaves as a pure capacitor
records.explanation: Correct: At resonance, X_L = X_C, so the net reactance = 0, giving impedance Z = R (its minimum value), and current = V/R (its maximum value), with power factor cos φ = R/Z = 1, meaning the circuit behaves as purely resistive. A is wrong because at resonance, impedance is actually MINIMUM and current is MAXIMUM — the opposite of what's stated. C is wrong because at resonance, the circuit behaves as a pure RESISTOR, not a capacitor. D is wrong because the power factor equals cos 0° = 1 at resonance (its maximum), not zero.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Capacitive reactance X_C is given by
records.explanation: Correct: X_C = 1/(2πfC) = 1/(ωC); it decreases as frequency increases, meaning a capacitor passes high-frequency AC more easily, with units of Ohms. A is wrong because 2πfC has the wrong units, giving F/s rather than Ω. C is wrong because 2πfL is actually the formula for inductive reactance, X_L, not capacitive. D is wrong because L/f is neither the capacitive nor inductive reactance formula.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Faraday's first law of electrolysis states that the mass of substance deposited at an electrode is
options: Inversely proportional to the time of electrolysis
Directly proportional to the quantity of charge (coulombs) passed through the electrolyte
Proportional to the temperature of the electrolyte
records.explanation: Correct: Faraday's 1st law states that mass ∝ Q = It, so the mass deposited is directly proportional to the quantity of electricity (current × time) passed, expressed as m = ZIt, where Z is the electrochemical equivalent. A is wrong because mass is DIRECTLY, not inversely, proportional to time at constant current. C is wrong because while temperature affects electrolyte conductivity generally, it isn't part of Faraday's 1st law itself. D is wrong because mass is in fact directly proportional to current at constant time, contradicting the claim of independence.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: In electrolysis of copper sulfate solution using copper electrodes, at the anode
options: Copper dissolves into solution, replenishing copper ions
records.explanation: Correct: With copper electrodes and CuSO₄ solution, at the cathode Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu (copper is deposited), while at the anode Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ (copper dissolves); the solution composition remains the same, which is the basis of electroplating and copper refining. A is wrong because copper is deposited at the CATHODE, not the anode. B is wrong because hydrogen gas is released only when platinum electrodes and dilute H₂SO₄ are used, not with copper electrodes. D is wrong because oxygen is released at the anode specifically when platinum electrodes and H₂SO₄ are used — not in this copper-electrode setup.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Thermionic emission is the release of electrons from a heated metal. The minimum energy required to release an electron from a metal surface is called
