records.explanation: Pressure = Force/Area. The force is constant (weight). Pressure is greatest when the area is smallest — standing on the toes of one foot.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Gases conduct electricity under
records.explanation: Gases conduct electricity at low pressure (so electrons can travel without collisions) and high voltage (to ionise the gas).

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The mass of a nucleus is the
options: Total number of its protons & neutrons
Total number of its protons & electrons
records.explanation: The mass number (nucleon number) is the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Three resistors with resistance 200Ω, 500Ω and 1kΩ are connected in series. A 6V battery is connected to either end of the combination. Calculate the potential difference between the ends of 200Ω resistance.
records.explanation: Total resistance = 200 + 500 + 1000 = 1700Ω. Current = V/R = 6/1700 = 0.00353A. Voltage across 200Ω = IR = 0.00353 × 200 = 0.706V ≈ 0.71V.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: An a.c of 1A at a frequency of 800 cycles per second flows through a coil, the inductance of which is 2.5mH and the resistance of which is 5Ω. What is the power absorbed in the Coil?
records.explanation: Power absorbed in a resistor is P = I²R = 1² × 5 = 5W. The inductor does not dissipate power (ideally).

records.subject: Physics
records.question: In semi-conductor, the carriers of current at room temperature are
records.explanation: In semiconductors at room temperature, both electrons and holes contribute to current conduction.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Water and Kerosene are drawn respectively into the two limbs of a Hare's apparatus. The density of water is 1.0gcm⁻³ and the density of kerosine is 0.80gcm⁻³. If the height of the water column is 20.0cm, calculate the height of the kerosine column.
records.explanation: In Hare's apparatus, ρ₁h₁ = ρ₂h₂. 1.0 × 20 = 0.8 × h₂ → h₂ = 20/0.8 = 25 cm.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: One newton × One meter equals?
records.explanation: 1 N × 1 m = 1 J (Joule), which is the unit of work or energy.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A single force which produces the same effect as a set of forces acting together at a point is known as the
records.explanation: The resultant force is a single force that produces the same effect as a system of forces.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Calculate the velocity ratio of a screw jack of pitch 0.2cm if the length of the tommy bar is 23cm

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The Earth's magnetic equator passes through Jos in Nigeria. At Jos, the
options: Horizontal component of the Earth's field is zero
records.explanation: At the magnetic equator, the angle of dip is zero (magnetic field is horizontal).

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Any line or section taken through an advancing wave in which all the particles are in the same phase is called the
records.explanation: A wave front is a line or surface connecting points that are in the same phase of vibration.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The point at which the molecules of a loaded wire begin to slide across each other resulting in a rapid increase in extension is
records.explanation: The yield point is where the material begins to deform plastically, with molecules sliding past each other and extension increasing rapidly.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The lower fixed point of a faulty thermometer reads 2°C while the upper fixed point is 100°C. What is the true temperature when the thermometer reads 51°C?
records.explanation: True temperature = (reading - lower_error)/(upper_error - lower_error) × 100. Lower error = 2°C, upper error = 100°C (so range = 98°C). True = (51 - 2)/98 × 100 = 49/98 × 100 = 50°C.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: If a body moves with a constant speed and at the same time undergoes an acceleration, its motion is said to be
records.explanation: In circular motion, a body can move at constant speed but still have acceleration (centripetal) due to changing direction.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The following are some units I. Ns II. Non III. Nm⁻² IV. JK⁻¹ V. JKg⁻¹ What are the units of latent heat?
records.explanation: Latent heat is energy per unit mass, so the unit is J/kg (JKg⁻¹).

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Which of these is observed when air is pumped out of a discharge tube without lowering its pressure
options: The conductivity of the air increases
The conductivity of the air decreases
records.explanation: Pumping out air reduces the number of charge carriers, so conductivity decreases (unless pressure is reduced to a point where mean free path increases, but the question says without lowering pressure).

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Which of the following characteristics of a wave is used in the measurement of the depth of the Sea?
records.explanation: Echo sounding (sonar) uses the reflection of sound waves from the sea bed to measure depth.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: If the attraction of the sun is suddenly ceased, the earth would continue to move in a straight line making a tangent with the original orbit. This statement is derived from Newton's
records.explanation: Newton's first law (inertia) states that a body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Heat may be transferred by conduction, convection and radiation. By which of these methods does heat travel through vacuum?
records.explanation: Radiation is the only mode of heat transfer that does not require a medium; it can travel through vacuum.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The part of the human eye that does similar work as the diaphragm of a camera lens is the
records.explanation: The iris controls the amount of light entering the eye, similar to the diaphragm in a camera.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A projectile of mass 4kg is fired vertically and reaches a maximum height of 40m. Calculate the potential energy at the highest point (g = 10ms⁻²)

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The length of the seconds hand of a laboratory clock is 0.1m. Calculate the speed at the top of the seconds hand
records.explanation: Seconds hand completes one revolution in 60s. Speed = circumference/time = 2πr/T = 2π×0.1/60 = 0.628/60 = 0.01047 ≈ 1.05×10⁻² m/s.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Work done on an object to bring it to a certain point in space is called
records.explanation: Potential energy is the energy stored in an object due to its position or configuration.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A copper rod, 5m long, when heated through 10°C, expands by 1mm. If a second copper rod, 2.5m long, is heated through 5°C, by how much will it expand?
records.explanation: Expansion is proportional to length and temperature change. For first rod: ΔL₁ = L₁ α ΔT₁ → 1mm = 5 × α × 10 → α = 0.02 mm/(m°C). For second: ΔL₂ = 2.5 × 0.02 × 5 = 0.25 mm.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A safety precaution designed to prolong the life of a lead acid accumulator is
options: By topping up the cells with concentrated acid
The use of naked flame when charging the battery
Keeping the specific gravity of the electrolyte within specified range
By connecting wires to the terminals directly when testing the level of charging
records.explanation: Maintaining the specific gravity of the electrolyte within the specified range helps prolong the life of a lead-acid accumulator.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The mass of water vapour in a given volume of air is 0.05g at 20°C, while the mass of water vapour required to saturate it at the same temperature is 0.15g. Calculate the relative humidity of the air.
records.explanation: Relative humidity = (mass of water vapour present / mass required for saturation) × 100 = (0.05/0.15) × 100 = 33.33%.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The angular dispersion of a prism depends on
options: The angle of incidence as well as the index of refraction
The thickness of the prism only
records.explanation: Angular dispersion depends on both the refractive index of the prism material and the angle of incidence (which affects the path length through the prism).

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Which of the following statements are correct of the production and propagation of waves? I. vibration produces waves II. waves transmit energy along the medium III. the medium through which the wave travels does not travel with the wave IV. waves do not require any medium for transmission
records.explanation: I, II, and III are correct: vibration produces waves, waves transmit energy, and the medium does not travel with the wave. IV is false because mechanical waves require a medium.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: An object is acted upon by a system of parallel forces causing the object to be in state equilibrium. Which of the following statement is not correct
options: The resultant of the parallel forces is zero
The algebraic sum of all the moments of the forces is zero
All the parallel forces must not be equal in magnitude and direction
The sum of forces in one direction must be equal to the sum of forces in the opposite direction
records.explanation: For equilibrium, the resultant force must be zero and the sum of moments zero. It is not necessary that all parallel forces be equal; they can be different as long as they balance. The incorrect statement is that all forces must not be equal — they can be equal.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct for a freely falling body? I. the total energy is entirely kinetic II. the ratio of potential energy to kinetic energy is constant III. the sum of potential and kinetic energy is constant
records.explanation: For a freely falling body, the sum of potential and kinetic energy is constant (conservation of mechanical energy). The ratio is not constant, and the total energy is not entirely kinetic except at the ground.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Efficiency of conduction in liquids and gases compared to solids is
records.explanation: Liquids and gases are poor conductors compared to solids (especially metals) because their molecules are farther apart.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A well 1km deep is filled with a liquid of density 950kg/m³ and g = 10m/s², the pressure at the bottom of the well is

records.subject: Physics
records.question: "Sum of all forces acting on a body is zero." This condition represents equilibrium'
records.explanation: The first condition for equilibrium is that the vector sum of all forces acting on the body is zero.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The volume of a stone having an irregular shape can be determined using?
records.explanation: The volume of an irregularly shaped solid can be determined using a measuring cylinder by the displacement method (water displacement).

records.subject: Physics
records.question: In Sunlight, a blue flower looks blue because we see the flower by the light it
records.explanation: A blue flower appears blue because it reflects blue light while absorbing most of the other colours in white sunlight. The colour we see is therefore mainly the wavelength reflected to our eyes.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A body moves in SHM between two point 20m on the straight line Joining the points. If the angular speed of the body is 5 rad/s. Calculate its speed when it is 6m from the center of the motion.
records.explanation: The 20 m distance is the full amplitude range, so the amplitude is 10 m. For SHM, v = ω√(A² − x²) = 5√(10² − 6²) = 5 × 8 = 40 m/s.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The equilibrium position of objects in any field corresponds to situation of
records.explanation: A stable equilibrium position corresponds to minimum potential energy. If the object is displaced slightly, its potential energy rises and a restoring effect tends to return it.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A mass of 0.5kg is whirled in a vertical circle of radius 2m at a steady rate of 2 rev/s. Calculate the centripetal force
records.explanation: The angular speed is ω = 2πf = 4π rad/s. Centripetal force is F = mrω² = 0.5 × 2 × (4π)² = 16π² ≈ 158 N.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A body was slightly displaced from its equilibrium position. Which one of the following is a condition for its stable equilibrium
options: an increase in the kinetic energy of the body
an increase in the potential energy of the body
a decrease in the kinetic energy of the body
an increase in the height of the body
records.explanation: When a body is displaced slightly from stable equilibrium, its potential energy increases. The system then tends to return to the original minimum-potential-energy position.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Which of the following readings cannot be determined with a meter rule?
records.explanation: A standard meter rule has a smallest division of 1 mm, or 0.1 cm, so readings are normally recorded to one decimal place in centimetres. A reading such as 2.56 cm requires a finer instrument.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Which of the following is consistent with Charles' law?
records.explanation: Charles' law states that at constant pressure, the volume of a fixed mass of gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature. The source's correct graph is option I. 0

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A few grains of table salt were put in a cup of cold water, kept at constant temperature and left undistributed. Eventually all the water tested salty. This action is due to?
records.explanation: Diffusion is the spontaneous movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to regions of lower concentration. The salt particles therefore spread throughout the water even without stirring.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The force required to make an object of mass m, travelling with velocity v, turn in a circle of radius r is
records.explanation: The required inward force is centripetal force, given by F = mv²/r. It increases with mass and the square of speed, but decreases as the radius increases.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A machine gun with a mass of 5kg fires a 50g bullet at a speed of 100 ms⁻¹. The recoil speed of the machine gun is
records.explanation: Initially the total momentum is zero. After firing, 0.05 × 100 = 5 kg m/s of forward momentum belongs to the bullet, so the gun must have 5 kg m/s backward momentum. Its recoil speed is 5/5 = 1 m/s.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: If in a simple pendulum experiment the length of the inextensible string is increased by a factor of four, its period is increased by a factor of?
records.explanation: For a simple pendulum, T = 2π√(L/g), so the period is proportional to √L. Increasing L by four therefore increases T by √4 = 2.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: In what range of temperature is the expansion of water anomalous?
records.explanation: Water behaves anomalously between 0°C and 4°C. As water is heated through this range, it contracts rather than expanding normally, reaching maximum density at 4°C.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Which of the following statements about radioactivity is true? (i) Alpha particle is positively charged (ii) Beta particle is negatively charged (iii) Gamma ray is neutral (iv) Beta particle has the same mass as helium atom (v) Gamma ray is charged.
records.explanation: Alpha particles are positively charged, beta particles are negatively charged in beta-minus emission, and gamma rays are neutral electromagnetic radiation. A beta particle is an electron, not a helium atom, and gamma rays have no charge.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Which of the following statements on the use of X-rays is incorrect? X-rays are used
options: In a hospital to obtain photographs of tissues and bones in the body
For the treatment of malignant growths like cancer cells
To reveal hidden flaws in metal castings and welded joints work of art
records.explanation: X-rays are used in medical imaging, radiotherapy and industrial radiography. Detecting fingerprints is not a standard application of X-rays.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: If a source of sound is moving, a stationary listener will hear a sound of different frequency. This is called?
records.explanation: The Doppler effect is the apparent change in observed frequency caused by relative motion between the source and observer.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Which of the following can be described as high tension transmission?
records.explanation: Electrical power is transmitted at high voltage and relatively low current. For a given power, increasing voltage reduces current and therefore reduces I²R energy losses in transmission lines.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The mass of a proton is approximately equal to that of
records.explanation: A proton and neutron have approximately equal masses, each close to 1 atomic mass unit. An electron is much lighter.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A transformer has 300 turns of wire in the primary coil and 30 turns in the secondary coil. If the input voltage is 100 volts, the output voltage is
records.explanation: For an ideal transformer, Vs/Vp = Ns/Np. Thus Vs/100 = 30/300 = 0.1, giving an output voltage of 10 V.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A solid weighs 4.8g in air, 2.8g in water and 3.2g in Kerosine. The ratio of density of the solid to that of the kerosine is
records.explanation: Loss of weight in water is 4.8 − 2.8 = 2.0 g, while loss in kerosine is 4.8 − 3.2 = 1.6 g. Since the loss is proportional to liquid density for the same displaced volume, the ratio of solid density to kerosine density is (4.8/2.0)/(1.6/2.0) = 3.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: When a sound wave passes from air into water its
options: speed and frequency increases but its wavelength remains the same
speed and wavelength increases but its frequency remains the same
speed increases but its frequency and wavelength decreases
records.explanation: The frequency is fixed by the source and does not change when the wave enters another medium. Sound travels faster in water, so with v = fλ and constant f, its wavelength also increases.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A convex mirror is used as a driving mirror because I. its image is erect II. It has a large field of view III. It has a long focal length Identify the CORRECT statement(s)
records.explanation: A convex mirror produces an erect, diminished image and provides a wide field of view, which is why it is useful as a driving mirror. A long focal length is not the reason given for its use.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A magnetic needle is suspended first at the earth's north magnetic pole and then at a point on the magnetic equator. The respective angles between the needle and the horizontal are
records.explanation: At the magnetic poles, the Earth's magnetic field is vertical, so the angle of dip is 90°. At the magnetic equator, the field is horizontal, so the angle of dip is 0°.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The refractive index of a liquid is 1.5. If the velocity of light in vacuum is 3.0 × 10⁸ ms⁻¹, the velocity of light in the liquid is
records.explanation: Refractive index n = c/v. Therefore v = c/n = (3.0 × 10⁸)/1.5 = 2.0 × 10⁸ m/s.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A ship travelling towards a cliff receives the echo of its whistle after 3.5 seconds. A short while later, it receives the echo after 2.5 seconds. If the speed of sound in air under the prevailing condition is 250 ms⁻¹, how much closer is the ship to the cliff?
records.explanation: For an echo, the sound travels to the cliff and back, so distance = vt/2. The change in distance is 250 × (3.5 − 2.5)/2 = 125 m.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Which of the following statements about defects of vision is/are CORRECT? I. For a long sighted person, close objects appear blurred II. For a short sighted person, distant objects appear blurred III. Short sight is corrected by using a pair of converging lenses
records.explanation: Long-sightedness makes nearby objects difficult to see clearly, while short-sightedness makes distant objects appear blurred. Short-sightedness is corrected with a diverging, not converging, lens.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Which of the following conditions are necessary and sufficient for total internal reflection to take place at the boundary between two optical media? I. Light is passing from optical denser medium to optically less dense medium II. Light is passing from optically less dense medium to optically denser medium III. Angle of incidence is greater than a certain critical value IV. Angle of incidence is lesser than a certain critical value
records.explanation: Total internal reflection requires light to travel from an optically denser medium to a less dense medium, with the angle of incidence greater than the critical angle.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The lower and upper fixed points marked on a Mercury-in-glass thermometer are 210mm apart. The end of the mercury column in the tube is 49mm above the lower fixed point in a room. What is the temperature of the room in degrees Celsius?
records.explanation: Using the fixed-point scale, T/100 = 49/210. Therefore T = 100 × 49/210 ≈ 23.3°C.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Heat is supplied uniformly at the rate of 100W to 1.0 × 10⁻²kg of a liquid for 20 seconds. If the temperature of the liquid rises by 5°C, then the specific heat capacity of the liquid is
records.explanation: The heat supplied is Q = Pt = 100 × 20 = 2000 J. Using Q = mcΔT, c = 2000/(0.01 × 5) = 4.0 × 10⁴ Jkg⁻¹K⁻¹.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Which of the following instruments consumes the highest current? I. Electric iron II. Television set III. Torchlight IV. Immersion heater 250V 220V 6V 110V 1kW 110W 30W 500W
records.explanation: Use I = P/V. The currents are 4 A, 0.5 A, 5 A and about 4.55 A respectively, so the torchlight has the highest current. 7

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Which of the following pairs is part of the electromagnetic spectrum? I. Radio waves II. sound waves III. Gamma rays IV. water waves
records.explanation: Radio waves and gamma rays are both electromagnetic waves. Sound waves and ordinary water waves are mechanical waves and require a medium.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A substance has half life of 3 min. After 6 min, the count rate was observed to be 400. What was its count rate at zero time?
records.explanation: Six minutes represents two half-lives. Therefore the original count rate was reduced by a factor of 2² = 4. Initial count rate = 400 × 4 = 1600. 9

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The slope of the straight line displacement-time graph indicates?
records.explanation: The slope of a displacement-time graph is Δdisplacement/Δtime, which is velocity. A straight line has constant slope, so it represents uniform velocity. 10

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A man will exert the greatest pressure when he?
options: stands on the toes of one foot
records.explanation: Pressure is P = F/A. The man's weight provides approximately the same force in each position, so the greatest pressure occurs when the contact area is smallest: standing on the toes of one foot. 11

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Two divers G and H are at depths 20m and 40m, respectively below the water surface in a lake. The pressure on G is p1 while the pressure on H is P2, If the atmospheric pressure is equivalent to 10m of water, then the value of P2/P1 is?
records.explanation: Including atmospheric pressure, the effective water depths are 20 + 10 = 30 m and 40 + 10 = 50 m. Therefore P2/P1 = 50/30 ≈ 1.67.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: One of the following readings represents the measurement of the length of a metal rod using vernier callipers. Taking the reading accuracy into consideration, the most likely one is
records.explanation: The expected precision of the vernier caliper in this question is to two decimal places, making 5.16 cm the appropriate reading.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Which of the units of the following physical quantities are derived? I. Area II. Thrust III. Pressure IV. Mass
records.explanation: Area, thrust and pressure are derived quantities. Mass is a fundamental SI quantity.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The motion of a body is simple harmonic if the?
options: acceleration is always directed towards a fixed point
path of motion is a straight line
acceleration is proportional to the square of the distance from a fixed point
acceleration is constant and directed towards a fixed point
records.explanation: In simple harmonic motion, acceleration is directed toward the equilibrium position and is proportional to displacement. Among the options, A captures the restoring nature of the acceleration.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Which of the following is not correct about the molecules of a substance in a gaseous state. They?
options: are in a constant state of motion
have a temperature which is measured by the average kinetic energy
The collision between the gases is perfectly inelastic
records.explanation: Gas molecules are in continuous random motion and have a distribution of speeds. In the ideal-gas model, collisions are perfectly elastic, not inelastic.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A given mass of gas has a pressure of 80 Nm^-2 at a temperature of 47 C. If the temperature is reduced to 27 C with volume remaining constant, the new pressure is?
records.explanation: At constant volume, P/T is constant. Convert to kelvin: 47°C = 320 K and 27°C = 300 K. Thus P2 = 80 × 300/320 = 75 Nm^-2.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: 0.5kg of water at 10ºC is completely converted to ice at 0ºC by extracting 88000J of heat from it. If the specific heat capacity of water is 4200Jkg^-1C^-1. Calculate the specific latent heat of fusion of ice.
records.explanation: First cool the water to 0°C: Q = mcΔT = 0.5 × 4200 × 10 = 21000 J. The remaining 67000 J removes the latent heat, so L = 67000/0.5 = 134000 J/kg = 134 kJ/kg.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Which of the following instruments may be used to measure relative humidity?
records.explanation: A hygrometer is used to measure the moisture content or relative humidity of air.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A source of sound produces waves in air of wavelength 1.65m. If the speed of sound in air is 330ms^-1, the period of vibration in air is?
records.explanation: Using v = fλ, f = 330/1.65 = 200 Hz. Therefore T = 1/f = 1/200 = 0.005 s.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A ball of mass 0.5kg moving at 10ms^-1 collides with another ball of equal mass at rest. If the two balls move off together after the impact, calculate their common velocity.
records.explanation: Because the balls move together after impact, momentum is conserved: 0.5(10) + 0.5(0) = (0.5 + 0.5)v. Therefore v = 5.0ms^-1.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A boy standing some distance from the foot of a tall cliff claps his hands and hears an echo 0.5s later. If the speed of sound is 340ms^-1, how far is he from the cliff?
records.explanation: The 0.5s is the time for the sound to travel to the cliff and back, so the total distance is 340 × 0.5 = 170m. The one-way distance to the cliff is therefore 170/2 = 85m.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A certain radioactive source emits radiation that was found to be deflected by both magnetic and electric fields. The radiation is?
records.explanation: Beta radiation consists of charged particles, so it can be deflected by both electric and magnetic fields. Gamma rays, X-rays and ultraviolet radiation are electromagnetic and are not deflected this way.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A particle of mass 10^-2kg is fixed to the tip of a fan blade which rotates with angular velocity of 100 rad s^-1. If the radius of the blade is 0.2m, the centripetal force is?
records.explanation: For rotational motion, F = mω²r. Thus F = 10^-2 × 100² × 0.2 = 20N.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A lead bullet of mass 0.05kg is fired with a velocity of 200ms^-1 into a block of mass 0.95kg. Given that the lead block can move freely, the final kinetic energy after impact is?
records.explanation: The bullet embeds in the block, so momentum is conserved. Initial momentum is 0.05 × 200 = 10kgm/s. The combined mass is 1kg, giving a final speed of 10m/s. Therefore KE = ½ × 1 × 10² = 50J. The source options therefore appear inconsistent; the calculated result is 50J.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A ball of mass 0.1kg is thrown vertically upwards with a speed of 10ms^-1 from the top of a tower 10m high. Neglecting air resistance, its total energy just before hitting the ground is? (Take g = 10ms^-2)
records.explanation: The initial kinetic energy is ½mv² = ½ × 0.1 × 100 = 5J. The initial gravitational potential energy is mgh = 0.1 × 10 × 10 = 10J. Total mechanical energy is therefore 15J and remains constant.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: When the brakes in a car are applied, the frictional force on the tyres is?
options: a disadvantage because it is in the direction of the motion of the car
a disadvantage because it is in the opposite direction of the motion of the car
an advantage because it is in the direction of the motion of the car
an advantage because it is in the opposite direction of the motion of the car
records.explanation: Braking requires friction to oppose the motion of the car and reduce its speed. Therefore the frictional force is an advantage during braking and acts opposite to the motion.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: If the stress on a wire is 10^7 Nm^-2 and the wire is stretched from its original length of 10.00m to 10.05m. The Young's modulus of the wire is?
records.explanation: Young's modulus = stress/strain. The strain is (10.05 − 10.00)/10.00 = 0.005. Therefore Y = 10^7/0.005 = 2.0 × 10^9 Nm^-2.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A solid weighs 10.00N in air, 6N when forcefully immersed in water, and 7.0N when fully immersed in a liquid, X. Calculate the relative density of the liquid X.
records.explanation: Upthrust in water = 10 − 6 = 4N, while upthrust in liquid X = 10 − 7 = 3N. Relative density = upthrust in X/upthrust in water = 3/4.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: When the temperature of a liquid increases, its surface tension
records.explanation: Increasing temperature increases molecular agitation and weakens the effective cohesive forces at the surface, so surface tension decreases.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A gas at a volume of V0 in a container at pressure p0 is compressed to one-fifth of its volume. What will be its pressure if the magnitude of its original temperature T is constant?
records.explanation: At constant temperature, Boyle's law gives pV = constant. Reducing the volume to V0/5 makes the pressure five times larger: p = 5p0.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A piece of substance of specific heat capacity 450Jkg^-1K^-1 falls through a vertical distance of 20m from rest. Calculate the rise in temperature of the substance on hitting the ground when all its energy is converted into heat. [g = 10ms^-2]
records.explanation: The lost gravitational potential energy becomes heat: mgh = mcΔT. Mass cancels, giving ΔT = gh/c = (10 × 20)/450 = 4/9ºC.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: I. A liquid boils when its saturated vapor pressure is equal to the external pressure II. Dissolved substances in pure water lead to an increase in the boiling point. III. When the external pressure is increased, the boiling point increases. IV. Dissolved substances in pure water decreases the boiling point. Which of the above combinations are peculiarities of the boiling point of a liquid?
records.explanation: Boiling occurs when saturated vapour pressure equals external pressure. Dissolved substances generally raise the boiling point, and increasing external pressure also raises the boiling point. Statement IV is therefore false.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The temperature gradient across a copper rod of thickness 0.02m, maintained at two temperature junctions of 20º and 80ºC respectively is?
records.explanation: Temperature gradient = temperature difference/thickness = (80 − 20)/0.02 = 60/0.02 = 3000 K m^-1.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Calculate the mass of ice that would melt when 2kg of copper is quickly transferred from boiling water to a block of ice without heat loss (specific heat capacity of copper = 400Jkg^-1K^-1, latent heat of fusion of ice = 3.3 x 10^5Jkg^-1).
records.explanation: The copper cools from 100ºC to 0ºC, releasing Q = mcΔT = 2 × 400 × 100 = 80000J. This melts mass m = Q/L = 80000/(3.3 × 10^5) = 8/33kg.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The equation of a wave traveling along the positive x-direction is given by; y = 0.25 x 10^-3 sin (500t - 0.025x). Determine the angular velocity of the wave motion.
records.explanation: Compare the equation with y = A sin(ωt − kx). The coefficient of t is the angular frequency, so ω = 500 rad s^-1.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: If a sound wave goes from a cold air region to a hot air region, its wavelength will?
records.explanation: The speed of sound increases with temperature. Since the frequency remains fixed at the boundary, λ = v/f means the wavelength increases.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The lowest note emitted by a stretched string has a frequency of 40Hz. How many overtones are there between 40Hz and 180Hz?
records.explanation: The fundamental is 40Hz and harmonics are 80Hz, 120Hz, 160Hz, 200Hz. Between 40Hz and 180Hz, the overtones are 80Hz, 120Hz and 160Hz: three overtones.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A man stands 4m in front of a plane mirror. If the mirror is moved 1m towards the man, the distance between him and his new image is?
records.explanation: The mirror moves from 4m to 3m from the man. A plane-mirror image is the same distance behind the mirror, so the image is 3m behind it. Man-to-image distance is therefore 3 + 3 = 6m.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The velocities of light in air and glass are 3.0 x 10^8ms^-1 and 2.0 x 10^8ms^-1 respectively. If the angle of refraction is 30º, the sine of the angle of incidence is?
records.explanation: Using n1 sin i = n2 sin r and n = c/v, we get sin i = (v_air/v_glass)sin r = (3/2)(0.5) = 0.75.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: An astronomical telescope is said to be in normal adjustment when the?
options: focal length of an object lens is longer than that of eye piece
final image is at the near point of eye
records.explanation: In normal adjustment, the objective forms an intermediate image at the eyepiece's focal point, so the final image is formed at infinity and the eye is relaxed.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A 2H inductor has negligible resistance and is connected to a 50/π Hz A.C supply. The reactance of the inductor is?
records.explanation: Inductive reactance is XL = 2πfL. Substituting f = 50/π Hz and L = 2H gives XL = 2π × 50/π × 2 = 200Ω.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Which of these is a derived unit?
records.explanation: Newton is a derived SI unit because 1N = 1kg m s^-2. Kilogram, metre and second are base SI units.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A bar magnet is divided into two pieces, which of the following statement is correct?
options: the magnetic field of each separate piece becomes stronger
records.explanation: Cutting a bar magnet does not isolate a single pole. Each piece becomes a smaller magnet with its own north and south poles.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Consider the wave equation y = 5mm sin [1cm^-1 x - 60s^-1t]. The wave number is?
records.explanation: In the standard wave equation y = A sin(kx − ωt), the coefficient of x is the wave number k. Here k = 1.0cm^-1.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: An object 40 cm high is 30cm from the pinhole camera. If the height of the image formed is 20 cm. What is the distance of the image from the pinhole?
records.explanation: For a pinhole camera, image height/object height = image distance/object distance. Thus 20/40 = v/30, giving v = 15cm.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A bar magnet is placed near and lying along the axis of a solenoid connected to a galvanometer. The pointer of the galvanometer shows no deflection when?
options: the magnet is moved towards the stationary solenoid
the magnet is moved away from the stationary solenoid
the solenoid is moved away from the stationary magnet
records.explanation: An induced emf requires a change in magnetic flux through the solenoid. If there is no relative motion between the magnet and solenoid, the flux is constant and no current is induced.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Tyres are treaded to?
records.explanation: Treads improve grip between the tyre and road, especially by helping remove water and maintain effective contact.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The relationship between the coefficient of linear expansion α and volumetric expansion γ is-----------------
records.explanation: For an isotropic solid, the coefficient of cubical or volumetric expansion is approximately three times the coefficient of linear expansion: γ = 3α.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Which of the following is not a consequence of hydrogen bubbles covering the copper plate of a primary cell?
options: formation of hydrogen bubbles on the electrode
increase in the resistance of the cell
records.explanation: The formation of hydrogen bubbles is the cause of polarization rather than a consequence of the bubbles themselves. The bubbles increase internal resistance and cause polarization.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A cell whose internal resistance is 0.55Ω delivers a current of 4 A to an external resistor. The lost voltage of the cell is?
records.explanation: Lost voltage is the voltage across the internal resistance: V = Ir = 4 × 0.55 = 2.20V.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Which of the following liquid is a poor conductor of electricity?
records.explanation: Distilled water contains very few ions, so it conducts electricity poorly. Tap, drinking and seawater contain dissolved ions that improve conductivity.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: An isotope has an initial activity of 120 Bq. 6 days later its activity is 15 Bq. The half-life is?
records.explanation: The activity falls from 120 to 15 Bq: 120 → 60 → 30 → 15, which is three half-lives. Therefore 6 days ÷ 3 = 2 days. The source options are inconsistent; the calculated half-life is 2 days.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The secondary pigments consist of?
records.explanation: In subtractive colour mixing, the secondary pigments are cyan, magenta and yellow.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A person standing waist-deep in a swimming pool appears to have short legs because of light?
records.explanation: Light from the submerged portion bends as it passes from water into air. This refraction makes the underwater part appear raised and therefore the legs appear shorter.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A tuning fork having a frequency of 312 Hz emits a wave which has a wavelength of 1.10 m. Calculate the velocity of sound.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: When the plate area of a capacitor increases?
records.explanation: For a parallel-plate capacitor, C = εA/d. Increasing the plate area A therefore increases the capacitance.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A magnet relay is a device used for?
options: reading the magnitude of magnetic flux
controlling another circuit carrying larger current
records.explanation: A relay uses an electromagnet to operate a switch in another circuit, allowing a relatively small control current to control a larger current.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: According to kinetic molecular model in gases,
options: the particles are closely packed together; they occupy minimum space and are usually arranged in a regular pattern
the particles vibrate about fixed positions and are held together by strong intermolecular bonds
the molecules are very far apart and occupy all the spaces made available to them
the particles occur in clusters with molecules slightly further apart
records.explanation: Gas molecules are widely separated, move randomly and occupy the available volume of their container.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A current of 0.5 A flows through a resistor when connected to a 40 V battery. How much energy is dispatched in 2 minutes?
records.explanation: Electrical energy E = VIt. With t = 2 minutes = 120s, E = 40 × 0.5 × 120 = 2400J.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Which light source operates primarily based on stimulated emission of radiation?
records.explanation: A laser operates through stimulated emission, where excited atoms or molecules are induced to emit coherent photons. This is the key principle that distinguishes laser light production from ordinary light sources.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: When a spiral spring is compressed by an external force of 200 N, it stores 0.16 J of energy. What amount of energy will it store when compressed by an external force of 700 N?
records.explanation: For a spring obeying Hooke's law, elastic potential energy is proportional to the square of the applied force. Therefore E2/E1 = (700/200)^2, giving E2 = 0.16 × 12.25 = 1.96 J.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: If the specific gravity of a liquid is 0.76, calculate its density((ρ_w = 1000Kgm^-3)
records.explanation: Specific gravity = density of liquid/density of water. Therefore density = 0.76 x 1000 = 760kgm^-3.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: What is the pressure exerted by 4.5m^3 of gas at 17ºC in a cylinder if the number of moles is 8.3 moles? (R = 8.31 JK^-1mol^-1)

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A well-lagged thin metal rod of length 0.2 m has a temperature gradient of 416 K m^-1. If one end is at 233º C, what is the temperature at the other end?
records.explanation: The temperature difference is gradient × length = 416 × 0.2 = 83.2°C. Taking the other end as hotter gives 233 + 83.2 = 316.2°C, matching the intended option D.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A wooden block of relative density 0.4 floats in a liquid of density 1600 kg m^-3. What fraction of its volume is immersed?
records.explanation: The block density is 0.4 × 1000 = 400 kg m^-3. For a floating body, fraction immersed = density of body/density of liquid = 400/1600 = 0.25.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: How long will it take to heat 4 kg of water from 30ºC to 65ºC using an electric kettle taking 5 A from a 240 V supply? (Specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J kg^-1 K^-1)
records.explanation: Q = mcΔT = 4 × 4200 × 35 = 588000J. Power = VI = 240 × 5 = 1200W. Therefore t = Q/P = 490s.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The volume of a fixed mass of gas at 0º C is 200 m^3. What is its volume at 273º C at constant pressure?
records.explanation: At constant pressure, V is proportional to absolute temperature. Temperature doubles from 273K to 546K, so volume doubles from 200m^3 to 400m^3.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: 5400kJ of heat energy was lost when some amount of steam condensed to water for drinking purposes at 15º C. What is the quantity of water collected? [L_f = 2.26 × 10^6 Jkg^-1, c_w = 4200 Jkg^-1K^-1]
records.explanation: Each kilogram releases latent heat during condensation and then cools from 100°C to 15°C. Thus Q = m[2.26×10^6 + 4200(85)], giving m ≈ 2.06kg.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A boy uses a single string pulley system to lift a mass of 20kg moving with a velocity of 5ms^-1. What is the power developed by the boy if g = 10ms^-2?
records.explanation: Power = force × velocity. The lifting force is mg = 20×10 = 200N, so P = 200×5 = 1000W.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The volume of a 1 cm^3 metal ball increases by 0.0018 cm^3 when heated through temperature θ. If the linear expansivity of the ball is 2.0 x 10^-5 K^-1, find θ.
records.explanation: Cubical expansivity β = 3α = 6×10^-5K^-1. Using ΔV = βVΔT gives 0.0018 = 6×10^-5 × 1 × θ, so θ = 30°C.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A hydraulic press consists of two cylinders of cross-sectional radius r1 and r2. If a force of 200N applied to the smaller piston (r1), causes a force of 3200N to be transmitted onto the larger piston (r2). The ratio r1:r2 is?
records.explanation: Pascal's principle gives F1/A1 = F2/A2. Since area is proportional to r², r1/r2 = √(200/3200) = 1/4.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A Force 18 N pulls a 40 kg mass on a horizontal floor at 0.3 ms^-2. Find the coefficient of friction.
records.explanation: Net force = ma = 40×0.3 = 12N. Friction = 18−12 = 6N. Normal reaction = 400N, so μ = 6/400 = 0.015.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: I. The colour of light depends on its frequency II. When white light is dispersed by a triangular prism, yellow is deviated more than green III. Rainbows are formed when rains fall heavily. Which of the above statements is/are correct about dispersion and colours?
records.explanation: I is correct because colour depends on frequency. II is false because green is deviated more than yellow. III is false because rainbow formation involves refraction, dispersion and internal reflection, not simply heavy rainfall.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Photometer is used to measure
records.explanation: A photometer is an instrument used to measure or compare the intensity of light.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: As per Faraday's laws of electromagnetic induction, an e.m.f is induced in a conductor whenever
options: lies parallel to the magnetic flux
lies outside but close to a magnetic field
records.explanation: An emf is induced when the magnetic flux linked with a conductor changes. A conductor cutting magnetic flux is a standard way of producing that change.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: One of these is not the use of an electroscope
options: testing the type of charge on a charge body
detecting the pressure of charge on a charged body
producing electric charge in a body
records.explanation: An electroscope detects and investigates electric charge; it does not serve as a device for producing electric charge in a body.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The bursting of water pipes during very cold weather, when the water in the pipes form ice could be attributed to
records.explanation: Water expands when it freezes. In a confined pipe, this expansion produces large pressure that can burst the pipe.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The velocity ratio of an inclined plane at 60º to the horizontal is
records.explanation: For an inclined plane, velocity ratio = 1/sinθ. At 60°, VR = 1/sin60° ≈ 1.155.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The device for measuring the angle of dip is
records.explanation: A dip circle is used to measure the angle through which a magnetic needle dips relative to the horizontal.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The diaphragm in the camera is similar to what part of the eyes?
records.explanation: The camera diaphragm controls the aperture and therefore the amount of light entering. The iris performs the same function in the eye.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: An air force jet flying with a speed of 335m/s went past an anti-aircraft gun. How far is the aircraft 5s later when the gun was fired?
records.explanation: Distance = speed × time = 335 × 5 = 1675m.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Two points on a velocity-time graph have coordinates (2s, 5m/s) and (4s, 15m/s). Calculate the mean acceleration
records.explanation: Mean acceleration is Δv/Δt = (15 − 5)/(4 − 2) = 5m/s².

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Two capacitors of 0.0003μF and 0.0006μF are connected in series, find their combined capacitance.
records.explanation: For capacitors in series, 1/C = 1/C1 + 1/C2. Therefore C = (0.0003 × 0.0006)/(0.0003 + 0.0006) = 0.0002μF.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: An accumulator is 90% efficient. If it gives out 2700J of energy while discharging, how much energy does it take in?
records.explanation: Efficiency = useful output/input. Therefore input energy = 2700/0.90 = 3000J.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Calculate the value of electric field intensity due to a charge of 4μC if the force due to the charge is 8N
records.explanation: Electric field intensity E = F/q = 8/(4 × 10^-6) = 2.0 × 10^6N/C.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: What is the colour of red rose under a blue light?
records.explanation: A red rose reflects red light and absorbs most other colours. Under blue illumination there is little or no red light available to reflect, so it appears black.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The efficiency of a cell with internal resistance of 2Ω supply current to a 6Ω resistor is
records.explanation: Cell efficiency = external resistance/(external resistance + internal resistance) = 6/(6 + 2) = 0.75 = 75%.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A force of 10N extends a spring of natural length 1m by 0.02m, calculate the length of the spring when the applied force is 40N.
records.explanation: By Hooke's law, extension is proportional to force. Quadrupling the force from 10N to 40N makes the extension 0.08m. Total length = 1 + 0.08 = 1.08m.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Bifocal lens is used to correct the eye defect of
records.explanation: Bifocal lenses provide different focal powers for near and distant vision and are commonly used to correct presbyopia.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A monochromatic light is one that
records.explanation: Monochromatic light consists essentially of one wavelength or one frequency.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The simple form of the lead acid accumulator often has a negative pole of
records.explanation: In a lead-acid accumulator, the negative plate is lead while the positive plate is lead peroxide.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: If the pressure on an enclosed gas is doubled and its temperature rises from 27ºC to 127ºC, then its volume will
records.explanation: Using PV/T = constant, V2/V1 = (T2/T1)(P1/P2) = (400/300)(1/2) = 2/3. Therefore the volume decreases by 1/3.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: If the displacement of a car is proportional to the square of time, then the car is moving with
records.explanation: If s is proportional to t², then s = kt². Differentiating twice with respect to time gives a constant acceleration.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The unit of impedance is
records.explanation: Impedance has the same SI unit as resistance: the ohm (Ω).

records.subject: Physics
records.question: I clear II sharp III poor IV dark Which of the above happens when the hole of a pinhole camera is diminished?
records.explanation: A smaller pinhole makes the image sharper and clearer, although it reduces brightness. Therefore I and II are the listed effects.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: When thermal energy in a solid is increased, the change in state is called
records.explanation: Adding thermal energy to a solid can cause it to change from solid to liquid; this change is called melting.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Newton's law of cooling is valid only for a
records.explanation: Newton's law of cooling is an approximation valid when the temperature difference between the body and its surroundings is relatively small.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A body is pulled on a horizontal surface with a rope inclined at 30º to the vertical. If the effective force pulling the body along the horizontal surface is 15N, calculate the tension on the rope.
records.explanation: The rope is 30° to the vertical, so it is 60° to the horizontal. Hence 15 = Tcos60°, giving T = 30N.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A particular household utilizes three electrical appliances for six hours daily if the appliances are rated 80W, 100W, and 120W respectively. Calculate the electrical bills paid monthly if an average month is 31 days. [1kwh = ₦24.08k]
records.explanation: Total power is 300W = 0.3kW. Daily energy is 0.3 × 6 = 1.8kWh and monthly energy is 55.8kWh. At ₦24.08 per kWh, the bill is about ₦1343.66.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: At a pressure of 10^5Nm^-2, a gas has a volume of 20m^3. Calculate the volume at 4 x 10^5Nm^-2 at constant temperature.
records.explanation: At constant temperature, PV is constant. Therefore V2 = (10^5 × 20)/(4 × 10^5) = 5m^3.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Calculate the upthrust on a spherical ball of volume 4.2 x 10^-4m^3 when totally immersed in a liquid of density 1028kgm^-3

records.subject: Physics
records.question: Calculate the magnetic force on an electron in a magnetic field of flux density 10T, with a velocity of 3 x 10^7m/s at 60º to the magnetic field (e = 1.6 x 10^-19C)

records.subject: Physics
records.question: A practical application of total internal reflection is found in
records.explanation: Optical fibres guide light through repeated total internal reflection.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: The land and sea breeze is attributed to
records.explanation: Land and sea breezes arise from convection caused by unequal heating of land and water.

records.subject: Physics
records.question: An effort of 40N is applied on a machine to lift a mass of 60kg. Determine the mechanical advantage of the machine [g = 10ms^-2]
records.explanation: Load = mg = 60 × 10 = 600N. Mechanical advantage = load/effort = 600/40 = 15.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question: Identify the CORRECTLY punctuated sentence:
options: The students who study hard pass their examinations.
The students, who study hard, pass their examinations.
The students who, study hard pass their examinations.
The students who study hard, pass their examinations.
records.explanation: Without commas, the relative clause 'who study hard' is restrictive (defining) — it specifies WHICH students pass. No commas are used for restrictive clauses. With commas (option B), it becomes non-restrictive, implying ALL students study hard.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question: Identify the sentence with CORRECT punctuation:
options: Its a pity that the boy failed his examination.
It's a pity that the boy failed his examination.
Its' a pity that the boy failed his examination.
Its a pity, that the boy failed his examination.
records.explanation: 'It's' (with apostrophe) is the contraction of 'it is'. 'Its' (without apostrophe) is the possessive pronoun. 'It's a pity' = 'It is a pity' — the apostrophe is required for contraction.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
options: Chidi's father, who is a lawyer is very strict.
Chidi's father who is a lawyer, is very strict.
Chidi's father, who is a lawyer, is very strict.
Chidi's father who is a lawyer is very strict.
records.explanation: 'Who is a lawyer' is a non-restrictive (non-defining) relative clause — it adds extra information and must be set off by two commas. The information is parenthetical.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question: Choose the sentence with CORRECT USE OF APOSTROPHE:
records.explanation: 'Children' is an irregular plural not ending in -s. For possessives of irregulars, add 's. So 'children's' is correct. For regular plurals ending in -s (e.g., students), only add an apostrophe after the -s: students'.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question: Which sentence demonstrates the CORRECT use of a semicolon?
options: He studied hard for the exam; and passed it.
He studied hard for the exam; he passed it easily.
He studied hard; for the exam.
He studied; hard for the exam.
records.explanation: A semicolon joins two independent clauses that are closely related in thought, WITHOUT using a conjunction. 'He studied hard for the exam; he passed it easily' has two independent clauses correctly joined by a semicolon.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question: Which vowel sound appears in both 'CUT' and 'LOVE'?
records.explanation: Both 'cut' /kʌt/ and 'love' /lʌv/ contain the short central vowel /ʌ/ despite different spellings. This is a JAMB favourite — testing vowel sound recognition across different spellings.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question: The letters 'TH' in the word 'THINK' represent the consonant sound _____.
records.explanation: 'Think' /θInk/ uses the voiceless dental fricative /θ/ — as in 'think', 'thank', 'thin'. The voiced version /ð/ appears in 'this', 'that', 'though'. JAMB tests this distinction heavily.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question: Which of the following is CORRECTLY stressed? (capital letters = stress)
records.explanation: 'Economy' /I'kɒnəmi/ has the primary stress on the second syllable: e-CON-o-my. This is one of JAMB's most repeated stress pattern questions.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question: Which of the following correctly shows the stress for 'deMOcracy'?
records.explanation: 'Democracy' /dI'mɒkrəsi/ has the primary stress on the SECOND syllable: de-MO-cra-cy.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question: The word 'cataSTROPhe' is INCORRECTLY stressed in option _____.
options: The word is correctly shown in A
records.explanation: 'Catastrophe' /kə'tæstrəfi/ has stress on the SECOND syllable: ca-TAS-tro-phe. Option A shows this correctly. Option C incorrectly places stress on the first syllable.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question: The plural of 'CURRICULUM' is _____.
records.explanation: 'Curriculum' is a Latin-origin noun. Its correct English plural (retaining the Latin form) is 'curricula'. JAMB tests Latin/Greek plurals: curriculum-curricula, criterion-criteria, phenomenon-phenomena.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word(s).

The principal took exception to the

ignoble

role the teacher played in the matter?
records.explanation: 'Ignoble' means dishonourable or base; its opposite is 'honourable'.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word(s).

The high cost of living these days calls for a lot of

frugality

?
records.explanation: 'Frugality' means careful, economical use of money; its direct opposite is 'extravagance' (wasteful spending).

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
The word in capital letters has the emphatic stress. Choose the option that best fits the expression in the sentence.

The university has been TEMPORARILY closed.
options: Has the campus been permanently closed?
Has the university been permanently open?
Has the university been permanently closed?
Has the college been temporarily closed?
records.explanation: The stress on TEMPORARILY signals a contrast with its opposite, 'permanently', while every other word in the sentence (subject 'university', verb 'closed') must stay unchanged.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).

I wonder what will be left of his essay when the

extraneous

material is deleted?
records.explanation: 'Extraneous' means irrelevant or not essential to the subject; 'irrelevant' is its nearest match.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.

One advantage of the English language in Nigeria is that it puts everyone ........ a common ........ ?
records.explanation: The fixed idiom is 'to put someone on a common footing' (i.e. on equal terms).

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
The passage below has gaps numbered 11 to 20. Immediately following each gap, four options are provided. Choose the most appropriate option for each gap.

It is the business of the scientist to accumulate knowledge about the universe and all that is in it and to find if he is able, common

……11…..[A. experiment B. instruments C. approaches D. factors]

which underlie and account for the facts that he knows. He chooses when he can, the method of the controlled

…….12…..[A. respondent B. experiment C. system D. data]

. If he wants to find out the effect of light on growing plants, he takes many plants, as alike as possible. Some he stands in the sun, some in the shade, some in the dark, all the time keeping all other

.....13.....[A. studies B. procedures C. objects D. conditions]

(temperature, moisture, nourishments) the same. In this way, by keeping other variables

……..14……[A. constant B. good C. dark D. natural]

and by varying the light only, the effect of light on plants can be clearly seen. This

…….15…..[A. research B. method C. tool D. rationale]

of using ‘controls’ can be applied to a variety of situations and can be used to find the answers to questions as widely different as ‘must moisture be present if

…….16….[A. an alloy B. gold C. bar D. iron]

is to rust?’ and which variety of beans give the greatest yield in one

……17…..[A. climate B. period C. season D. weather]?

In the course of his

……18…..[A. finding B. queries C. experiment D. inquiries]

, the scientist may find what he thinks is one common explanation for an increasing number of facts the explanation, if it seems consistently to fit the various facts, is called

…….19……[A. an antithesis B. a principle C. a thesis D. a hypothesis]

. If this continues to stand the test of numerous experiments and remains unshaken, it becomes a

……20…..[A. deduction B. law C. notion D. thesis].

In question number 15 above, choose the best option from letters A-D that best completes the gap.
records.explanation: The passage refers back to 'the method of the controlled experiment' described earlier, so 'method' is the word that logically continues that thread: 'This method of using controls...'.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the option that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the underlined letter(s).

Preach

ed

?
records.explanation: The '-ed' in 'preached' is pronounced /t/ (after the voiceless 'ch'). 'Walked' also ends with /t/ (after the voiceless 'k').

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word(s).

Tunde's reaction

underscores

the point I was making?
records.explanation: 'Underscores' means to emphasize or highlight; its opposite is 'minimizes' (to play down).

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.

Didn't ......... draw your attention to the entry requirements?
records.explanation: In questions (including rhetorical negative questions like this one), the prescriptive rule tested by JAMB favours 'any-' compounds over 'some-' compounds.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the option that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the underlined letter(s).

cou

gh

?
records.explanation: The 'gh' in 'cough' is pronounced /f/. 'Enough' also has 'gh' pronounced /f/.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question: Choose the option that has a different vowel sound from the others?
records.explanation: 'Dog', 'cough' and 'rot' all share the short vowel sound /ɒ/. 'Code' has the different diphthong /əʊ/.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).

They are considered to be legal

luminaries
records.explanation: 'Luminaries' means distinguished, eminent figures in a field; 'eminent experts' is the closest match.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).

Teachers of music believes in its

therap.eutic

effect?
records.explanation: 'Therapeutic' means having a healing effect; 'healing' is its nearest match.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
If our thoughts is to be clear and we are to succeed in communicating it to other people, we must have some method of fixing the meaning of the words we use. When we use a word whose meaning is not certain, we may well be asked to define it. There is a usual traditional device for doing this by indicating the class to which whatever is indicated by the term belongs and also other particular property which distinguishes it from all other members of the same class. Thus we may define a whale as a ‘marine animal that spouts’. ‘Marine animals’ in this definition indicates the general class to which the whale belongs and ‘spouts’ indicates the particular property that distinguishes whales from other such marine animals as fishes, seals, jellyfish and lobsters. In the same way, we can define an even number as a finite integer divisible by two or a democracy as a system of government in which the people themselves rule.

there are other ways, of course of indicating the meaning of words. We may for example, find it hard to make a suitable definition of the word ‘animal’, as we say that an animal is such a thing as a rabbit, dog fish or goat. Similarly, we may say that religion is such a system as Christianity, Islam, Judaism and Buddhism. This way of indicating the meaning of a term by enumerating examples of what it includes is obviously of limited usefulness. If we indicate our use of the word ‘animal’ as above, our hearers might for example be doubtful whether a sea-anemone or a slug was to be included in the class of animals. It is however, a useful way of supplementing a definition if the definition itself id definite without being easily understandable. Failure of an attempt at definition to serve its purpose may result from giving as distinguishing mark one which either does not belong to all the things the definition id intended to include, or does belong to some members of the same general class which the definition is intended to exclude.

The expression 'we may well be asked' as used in the passage means
options: the listener is always justified to ask questions
it is inconceivable that we will be asked
we can reasonably expect to be asked
records.explanation: 'May well be asked' expresses probability ('it is quite likely that...'), not certainty or impossibility.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Those who have been following the argument for and against the deregulation of the oil industry in Nigeria may have got the impression that deregulation connotes lack of control or indifference on the part of the government. But there is nothing so far from official quarters to suggest that deregulation will cause the government to relinquish its control of the oil industry because the absence of direct control does not mean that it will surrender all its rights to the entrepreneurs who may want to participate in the industry. Yet the opposition expressed so far against stems from the fear that the government would leave Nigerians at the mercy of a heartless cartel who would command the heights of the oil industry and cause pump price of fuel to rise above the means of most Nigerians.

`As a result of such fears, many Nigerians have become resentful of deregulation and in fact the Nigeria Labour Congress  (NLC) has threatened to ‘deregulate’ the government if it should go ahead with the deregulation plan. But Nigerians have not fared any better with the economy totally in government control. Until recently, the most important sectors of the economy were in the hands of the government. Today, the deregulation of some of these sectors has broken its monopoly and introduced healthy competition to make a little easier for Nigerians. A good example is the breaking of the stifling monopoly of Nigeria Airways. Today, the traveller is king at the domestic airports as opposed to the struggle that air travels used to be under Nigeria Airways monopoly. Before, it was almost easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for travellers to board a plane.

Following from this, the apostles of deregulation rightly heap all the blame for the problems associated with petroleum products distribution in this country squarely on the government, which owns all the refineries and which sells fuel to local consumers through its agency, the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC). In the same way, the government argues that if the current NNPC monopoly were broken with the introduction of entrepreneurs to the refining and sale of petroleum products in the country, the Nigerian people would be all the better for it. It stands to reason that once the government continues to fix maximum prices would be all the better for it. It stands to reason that once the government continues to fix maximum prices for petroleum products in this country, the deregulation of the oil sector should bring some relief to the people by ensuring that wastage, corruption and inefficiency are reduced to the minimum. Consumers will also have the last laugh because competition will result in the availability of the products at reasonable prices. This appears to be the sense in deregulation.

Which of these correctly summaries the arguments adduced by the advocate of deregulation?
options: dereuglating the economy will make the NNPC more efficient and less wasteful
the government should deregulate every aspect of the nigerian economy
breaking the NNPC's monopoly and introducing competition among entrepreneurs will reduce wastage, corruption and inefficiency and make petroleum products more available at reasonable prices
competition should be allowed in the production and distribution of petroleum products
records.explanation: The passage's pro-deregulation argument combines both the efficiency gain from breaking NNPC's monopoly AND the price/availability benefit from competition — option C is the only one that captures both parts of the argument.

records.question:
Recgnizing the need for objectivity in their work, the early report writers to develop a writing style which convey this attitude. They reasoned that the source of the subjective quality in a report is the human being.  And they reasoned that objectivity is best attained by emphasizing the factual material of a report rather 5than the personalities involved. So they worked to remove the human being from their writing. Impersonal writing style was the result. By impersonal writing is meant writing in the third person-without I’s, we’s or you’s.

In recent years, impersonal writing has been strenuously questioned by many writers. These writers point out that personal writing is more forceful and direct than is impersonal writing. They contend that writing which brings both reader and writer into the picture is more like conversation and therefore more interesting. And the answer to the point on objectivity when written in personal style as when in impersonal style. Frequently, they counter with the argument that impersonal writing leads to an overuse of passive voice and a generally dull writing style. This last argument however lacks substances. Impersonal writing can and should be interesting. Any dullness it may have is wholly the fault of the writer. As proof, one has only to look at the lovely styles used by the writers for newspapers, news magazines and journals. Most of this writing is impersonal and usually it is not dull.

As in most cases of controversy, there is some merit to the arguments on both sides. There are situations in which personal writing is best. There are situations in which impersonal writing is best. And there are situations in which either style is appropriate. The writer must decide at the outset of his work which style is best for his own situation.

Her decision should be based on the circumstances of each report situation. First, he should consider the expectations or desires of those for whom he is preparing the report. More than likely he will find a preference for impersonal style for like most human beings; businessman has been slow to break tradition. Next, the writer should consider the formality of the report situation. If the situation is informal, as when the report is really a personal communication of information between business associates, personal writing is appropriate. But if the situation is formal, as is case with most reports, the conventional impersonal style is best.

One argument given in support of personal writing is that it
options: is more forceful and direct than impersonal writing
can be more objective than impersonal writing
is the style to use in all situations involving businessmen
has informal features which make it more diverting than impersonal writing
records.explanation: The passage explicitly states this argument: 'personal writing is more forceful and direct than is impersonal writing.'

Those who have been following the argument for and against the deregulation of the oil industry in Nigeria may have got the impression that deregulation connotes lack of control or indifference on the part of the government. But there is nothing so far from official quarters to suggest that deregulation will cause the government to relinquish its control of the oil industry because the absence of direct control does not mean that it will surrender all its rights to the entrepreneurs who may want to participate in the industry. Yet the opposition expressed so far against stems from the fear that the government would leave Nigerians at the mercy of a heartless cartel who would command the heights of the oil industry and cause pump price of fuel to rise above the means of most Nigerians.

`As a result of such fears, many Nigerians have become resentful of deregulation and in fact the Nigeria Labour Congress  (NLC) has threatened to ‘deregulate’ the government if it should go ahead with the deregulation plan. But Nigerians have not fared any better with the economy totally in government control. Until recently, the most important sectors of the economy were in the hands of the government. Today, the deregulation of some of these sectors has broken its monopoly and introduced healthy competition to make a little easier for Nigerians. A good example is the breaking of the stifling monopoly of Nigeria Airways. Today, the traveller is king at the domestic airports as opposed to the struggle that air travels used to be under Nigeria Airways monopoly. Before, it was almost easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for travellers to board a plane.

Following from this, the apostles of deregulation rightly heap all the blame for the problems associated with petroleum products distribution in this country squarely on the government, which owns all the refineries and which sells fuel to local consumers through its agency, the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC). In the same way, the government argues that if the current NNPC monopoly were broken with the introduction of entrepreneurs to the refining and sale of petroleum products in the country, the Nigerian people would be all the better for it. It stands to reason that once the government continues to fix maximum prices would be all the better for it. It stands to reason that once the government continues to fix maximum prices for petroleum products in this country, the deregulation of the oil sector should bring some relief to the people by ensuring that wastage, corruption and inefficiency are reduced to the minimum. Consumers will also have the last laugh because competition will result in the availability of the products at reasonable prices. This appears to be the sense in deregulation.

competition resulting from deregulation should make petroleum products available to nigerians at reasonable prices

Recgnizing the need for objectivity in their work, the early report writers to develop a writing style which convey this attitude. They reasoned that the source of the subjective quality in a report is the human being.  And they reasoned that objectivity is best attained by emphasizing the factual material of a report rather 5than the personalities involved. In recent years, impersonal writing has been strenuously questioned by many writers. These writers point out that personal writing is more forceful and direct than is impersonal writing. They contend that writing which brings both reader and writer into the picture is more like conversation and therefore more interesting. And the answer to the point on objectivity when written in personal style as when in impersonal style. Frequently, they counter with the argument that impersonal writing leads to an overuse of passive voice and a generally dull writing style. This last argument however lacks substances. Impersonal writing can and should be interesting. Any dullness it may have is wholly the fault of the writer. As proof, one has only to look at the lovely styles used by the writers for newspapers, news magazines and journals. Most of this writing is impersonal and usually it is not dull.

As in most cases of controversy, there is some merit to the arguments on both sides. There are situations in which personal writing is best. There are situations in which impersonal writing is best. And there are situations in which either style is appropriate. The writer must decide at the outset of his work which style is best for his own situation.

Her decision should be based on the circumstances of each report situation. First, he should consider the expectations or desires of those for whom he is preparing the report. he is objective and fair in presenting both sides of the argument
