records.question:
If our thoughts is to be clear and we are to succeed in communicating it to other people, we must have some method of fixing the meaning of the words we use. When we use a word whose meaning is not certain, we may well be asked to define it. There is a usual traditional device for doing this by indicating the class to which whatever is indicated by the term belongs and also other particular property which distinguishes it from all other members of the same class. Thus we may define a whale as a ‘marine animal that spouts’. ‘Marine animals’ in this definition indicates the general class to which the whale belongs and ‘spouts’ indicates the particular property that distinguishes whales from other such marine animals as fishes, seals, jellyfish and lobsters. In the same way, we can define an even number as a finite integer divisible by two or a democracy as a system of government in which the people themselves rule.

there are other ways, of course of indicating the meaning of words. We may for example, find it hard to make a suitable definition of the word ‘animal’, as we say that an animal is such a thing as a rabbit, dog fish or goat. Similarly, we may say that religion is such a system as Christianity, Islam, Judaism and Buddhism. This way of indicating the meaning of a term by enumerating examples of what it includes is obviously of limited usefulness. If we indicate our use of the word ‘animal’ as above, our hearers might for example be doubtful whether a sea-anemone or a slug was to be included in the class of animals. It is however, a useful way of supplementing a definition if the definition itself id definite without being easily understandable. Failure of an attempt at definition to serve its purpose may result from giving as distinguishing mark one which either does not belong to all the things the definition id intended to include, or does belong to some members of the same general class which the definition is intended to exclude.

the writer uses the expression 'fixing the meaning of the words we use' to mean
options: establishing a precise and definite meaning for words to ensure clear communication
getting even with the people who always ask for definitions
repair the damage done by inadequate definition during communication
using definitionto help people build up their vocabulary
records.explanation: The passage opens by stating that for our thoughts to be clear and communicable, 'we must have some method of fixing the meaning of the words we use' -- meaning establishing a precise, definite meaning for words.

So they worked to remove the human being from their writing. Impersonal writing style was the result. By impersonal writing is meant writing in the third person-without I’s, we’s or you’s.

In recent years, impersonal writing has been strenuously questioned by many writers. These writers point out that personal writing is more forceful and direct than is impersonal writing. They contend that writing which brings both reader and writer into the picture is more like conversation and therefore more interesting. And the answer to the point on objectivity when written in personal style as when in impersonal style. Frequently, they counter with the argument that impersonal writing leads to an overuse of passive voice and a generally dull writing style. This last argument however lacks substances. Impersonal writing can and should be interesting. Any dullness it may have is wholly the fault of the writer. As proof, one has only to look at the lovely styles used by the writers for newspapers, news magazines and journals. Most of this writing is impersonal and usually it is not dull.

As in most cases of controversy, there is some merit to the arguments on both sides. There are situations in which personal writing is best. There are situations in which impersonal writing is best. And there are situations in which either style is appropriate. The writer must decide at the outset of his work which style is best for his own situation.

Her decision should be based on the circumstances of each report situation. First, he should consider the expectations or desires of those for whom he is preparing the report. More than likely he will find a preference for impersonal style for like most human beings; businessman has been slow to break tradition. Next, the writer should consider the formality of the report situation. If the situation is informal, as when the report is really a personal communication of information between business associates, personal writing is appropriate. But if the situation is formal, as is case with most reports, the conventional impersonal style is best.

From the passage, what determines the appropriateness of a style is the
records.explanation: The passage states the writer must base his decision on 'the circumstances of each report situation' -- weighing both audience expectations and the formality of the situation -- so the situation as a whole, not any single factor, determines appropriateness.

If our thoughts is to be clear and we are to succeed in communicating it to other people, we must have some method of fixing the meaning of the words we use. When we use a word whose meaning is not certain, we may well be asked to define it. There is a usual traditional device for doing this by indicating the class to which whatever is indicated by the term belongs and also other particular property which distinguishes it from all other members of the same class. Thus we may define a whale as a ‘marine animal that spouts’. ‘Marine animals’ in this definition indicates the general class to which the whale belongs and ‘spouts’ indicates the particular property that distinguishes whales from other such marine animals as fishes, seals, jellyfish and lobsters. In the same way, we can define an even number as a finite integer divisible by two or a democracy as a system of government in which the people themselves rule.

there are other ways, of course of indicating the meaning of words. We may for example, find it hard to make a suitable definition of the word ‘animal’, as we say that an animal is such a thing as a rabbit, dog fish or goat. Similarly, we may say that religion is such a system as Christianity, Islam, Judaism and Buddhism. This way of indicating the meaning of a term by enumerating examples of what it includes is obviously of limited usefulness. If we indicate our use of the word ‘animal’ as above, our hearers might for example be doubtful whether a sea-anemone or a slug was to be included in the class of animals. It is however, a useful way of supplementing a definition if the definition itself id definite without being easily understandable. Failure of an attempt at definition to serve its purpose may result from giving as distinguishing mark one which either does not belong to all the things the definition id intended to include, or does belong to some members of the same general class which the definition is intended to exclude.

effective communication requires a precise method of determining the meaning of the words used
every speaker or writer has a method of defining words
there are both traditional and modern methods of defining words
records.explanation: This follows directly from the passage's opening claim that clear thought and communication require 'some method of fixing the meaning of the words we use.'

records.question:
Those who have been following the argument for and against the deregulation of the oil industry in Nigeria may have got the impression that deregulation connotes lack of control or indifference on the part of the government. But there is nothing so far from official quarters to suggest that deregulation will cause the government to relinquish its control of the oil industry because the absence of direct control does not mean that it will surrender all its rights to the entrepreneurs who may want to participate in the industry. Yet the opposition expressed so far against stems from the fear that the government would leave Nigerians at the mercy of a heartless cartel who would command the heights of the oil industry and cause pump price of fuel to rise above the means of most Nigerians.

`As a result of such fears, many Nigerians have become resentful of deregulation and in fact the Nigeria Labour Congress  (NLC) has threatened to ‘deregulate’ the government if it should go ahead with the deregulation plan. But Nigerians have not fared any better with the economy totally in government control. Until recently, the most important sectors of the economy were in the hands of the government. Today, the deregulation of some of these sectors has broken its monopoly and introduced healthy competition to make a little easier for Nigerians. A good example is the breaking of the stifling monopoly of Nigeria Airways. Today, the traveller is king at the domestic airports as opposed to the struggle that air travels used to be under Nigeria Airways monopoly. Before, it was almost easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for travellers to board a plane.

Following from this, the apostles of deregulation rightly heap all the blame for the problems associated with petroleum products distribution in this country squarely on the government, which owns all the refineries and which sells fuel to local consumers through its agency, the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC). In the same way, the government argues that if the current NNPC monopoly were broken with the introduction of entrepreneurs to the refining and sale of petroleum products in the country, the Nigerian people would be all the better for it. It stands to reason that once the government continues to fix maximum prices would be all the better for it. It stands to reason that once the government continues to fix maximum prices for petroleum products in this country, the deregulation of the oil sector should bring some relief to the people by ensuring that wastage, corruption and inefficiency are reduced to the minimum. Consumers will also have the last laugh because competition will result in the availability of the products at reasonable prices. This appears to be the sense in deregulation.

Which of the following conclusions can be reached from the passage?
options: the deregulation of the economy will solve all the problems of petroleum products distribution
the government is hell-bent on leaving nigerians at the mercy of a heartless cartel
nigerians cannot buy fuel at exorbitant prices
deregulation of the oil sector could benefit consumers through competition and reduced inefficiency, leading to more reasonable prices
records.explanation: The passage concludes that competition arising from deregulation 'will result in the availability of the products at reasonable prices' and that wastage, corruption and inefficiency would be reduced -- directly supporting this conclusion.

records.explanation: The stress on EAGLES highlights that team specifically as the winner; the matching sentence keeps everything else the same and confirms it with a yes/no question: 'Did the Eagles win the match?'

records.subject: Use of English

Choose the

option nearest in meaning

to the word or phrase underlined.

Emeka's painting was so

realistic

that it could almost have been a photograph.
records.explanation: A 'realistic' painting looks true to life; among the options, 'authentic' (genuine, true-to-reality) is the nearest match.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the

option nearest in meaning

to the word or phrase underlined.

His

taciturnity

amazed everyone in the court during the legal tussle
records.explanation: 'Taciturnity' means habitual silence or reluctance to speak; 'reticence' is its precise synonym.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).

You can travel on your own ....?
records.explanation: The main clause uses the modal 'can' affirmatively, so the tag must be negative and repeat the same modal: 'can't you'.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).

I was often angry ....... Oche since he differed ....... me often?
records.explanation: 'Angry with' a person and 'differ with' someone (meaning to disagree) are both standard, correct collocations.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word(s).

The proprietor accused Uche of silently

acquiescing

to the students' demands?
records.explanation: 'Acquiescing' means passively complying; its opposite is 'resisting'.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word(s).

The teacher recounted two events that were

analogous with

each other.
records.explanation: 'Analogous' means similar or comparable; its opposite is 'different from'.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).

Yesterday, my mother asked me......
records.explanation: Reported yes/no questions use 'if'/'whether' plus normal statement word order, with the tense backshifted to match the past reporting verb: 'asked me if I was tired'.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the option

opposite in meaning

to the underlined word(s).

Asabe bought a

glossy

pair of shoes.
records.explanation: 'Glossy' means smooth and shiny; its opposite is 'rough and dull'.

records.question:
Choose the

option nearest in meaning

to the word or phrase underlined.

No wonder Sikemi later became a detective; she has been very

observant.
records.explanation: 'Observant' means quick to notice details; 'perceptive' is its nearest match.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the appropriate stress pattern from the options. The syllables are written in capital letters.

suburbanite
records.explanation: 'Suburbanite' is stressed on its second syllable: su-BUR-ban-ite.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the

option nearest in meaning

to the word or phrase underlined.

The accident victim received

a superficial

wound from the crash
records.explanation: A 'superficial' wound is one on the surface only, i.e. 'external', as opposed to a deep, internal injury.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.

If I visited England, I might go to Manchester City.
options: When I go to England , I could go to Manchester City
Whenever I visit England, I must go to Manchester City
I did not go to England and could  not go to Manchester
I could not visit Manchester City because I did not want to go to England
records.explanation: The second conditional ('if...might') expresses a hypothetical possibility contingent on visiting England; 'When I go to England, I could go to Manchester City' preserves this same England-then-possibly-Manchester relationship.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word(s).

The president can afford to dispense with some of his

henchmen.
records.explanation: 'Henchmen' are loyal, often unquestioning followers; their opposite is 'detractors' (critics/opponents).

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.

One thing I will not be complaining about in my new job is a lack of excitement?
options: The job is not too  exciting
The job has been previously done
records.explanation: 'Not complaining about a lack of excitement' is a double negative meaning there IS plenty of excitement, i.e. the job is exciting.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word(s).

Many Nigerian are

wary

of night journeys
records.explanation: 'Wary' means cautious or suspicious; its opposite is 'unscared of' (not afraid of).

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the

option nearest in meaning

to the word or phrase underlined.

The boxer

fizzled out

just in the sixth round
options: became tired but fought on spiritedly
records.explanation: 'Fizzled out' means to end weakly or disappointingly after a promising start, matching a boxer surrendering disappointingly.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).

You, who ...... convicted, should appeal.
records.explanation: The relative clause 'who ... convicted' refers back to 'you', so the verb must agree with 'you': 'are'.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).

The public library has stopped ........ books to readers?
records.explanation: Libraries 'lend' books to readers (hence 'lending library'); this is the standard verb for the service.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.

If the trader paid in full, his order was not pruned down.
options: The trader who made full payment did not have his order reduced
The trader who made some payment did not have his order delayed
Unless the trader paid  in full his order would be rejected
As the trader did not increase his order, he did not need to pay in full
records.explanation: 'Paid in full' and 'not pruned down' directly correspond to 'made full payment' and 'did not have his order reduced'.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word(s).

After fifty years, he could not find anyone who was

contemporary with

him at college.
records.explanation: 'Contemporary with' means existing at the same time as someone; its opposite is to be 'strange to' (unfamiliar with, as someone from a different era would be).

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).

As we sat ....... the silence, my eyes ....... the room?
records.explanation: 'Sat in the silence' and 'eyes roamed the room' are both natural, idiomatic collocations describing quiet stillness and eyes wandering.

records.subject: Use of English
records.question:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).

By the end of the football match today, we ...... the best player?
records.explanation: 'By the end of the match today' signals a future point by which something will be complete, requiring the future perfect: 'will have known'.

E(ng)lish

departmentalize?

records.question: Choose the option that has a different stress pattern from the others.

records.question:

option nearest in meaning

to the word or phrase underlined.

Courteously

, Ade stood back to let his teacher go first through the door
records.explanation: 'Courteously' means in a polite manner; 'politely' is its direct synonym.

records.question:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.

The class was tired of the new boy jawing away all the time?
options: He was always chewing in the class
He was always making trouble for the class
He talked continuously in the class
records.explanation: 'Jawing away' is informal slang for talking continuously/chattering.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.topic: Structural/functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
heldExamples.question: Which of the following correctly describes the adaptive significance of spines in cacti?
options: They trap insects for nutrient absorption
They are modified leaves that reduce water loss through transpiration
They increase photosynthetic surface area in dry environments
They provide support against strong desert winds
heldExamples.explanation: Cacti spines are modified leaves that have a very small surface area, drastically reducing the surface through which water is lost by transpiration. Photosynthesis occurs in the thick, fleshy green stem.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Which of the following organisms reproduces by binary fission?
heldExamples.explanation: Paramecium (a protozoan) reproduces asexually by binary fission — splitting into two identical daughter cells. This is the primary mode of asexual reproduction in most unicellular organisms.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: An organism with a notochord at some stage of its life is classified as a
heldExamples.explanation: All chordates possess a notochord (a flexible rod-like structure) at some stage of their development. Vertebrates are a subgroup of chordates where the notochord is replaced by a vertebral column.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Which of the following best describes the structural complexity of animals from coelenterates to mammals?
heldExamples.explanation: The evolutionary progression in animal complexity goes from the cellular level (coelenterates/sponges) → tissue level (flatworms) → organ level → organ system level (vertebrates including mammals).

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Which of the following statements about birds (Aves) is INCORRECT?
options: They have scales on their legs
They are the only vertebrates that lay eggs
heldExamples.explanation: Many vertebrates lay eggs — reptiles, fish, amphibians, and even some mammals (monotremes like the platypus) lay eggs. Birds are not the only egg-laying vertebrates.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: In photosynthesis, which of the following is a raw material (reactant)?
heldExamples.explanation: Carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere and water (H2O) from the soil are the two raw materials (reactants) in photosynthesis. Glucose and oxygen are the products.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Anaerobic respiration in yeast produces
heldExamples.explanation: During anaerobic fermentation by yeast: Glucose → Ethanol + Carbon dioxide. This is used in brewing and baking. (In muscles, anaerobic respiration produces lactic acid.)

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The process by which a pollen grain grows a tube to deliver male gametes to the ovule is called
heldExamples.explanation: After pollination, the pollen grain germinates on the stigma and grows a pollen tube (siphonogamy) down through the style to the ovule, delivering two male gametes — one fertilises the egg, the other fuses with polar nuclei (double fertilisation in angiosperms).

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Which of the following is an example of a reflex action?
options: Withdrawing a hand from a hot object
heldExamples.explanation: A reflex action is an automatic, involuntary, rapid response to a stimulus not requiring conscious thought. Withdrawing from pain (pain withdrawal reflex) is a classic spinal reflex arc.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
heldExamples.question: The relationship between nitrogen-fixing bacteria (Rhizobium) and leguminous plants is best described as
heldExamples.explanation: Rhizobium bacteria live in root nodules of legumes. The bacteria fix atmospheric nitrogen into usable forms for the plant; the plant provides organic carbon and shelter for the bacteria. Both benefit — this is mutualism.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: A Secchi disc is used in ecological studies to measure
heldExamples.explanation: A Secchi disc is a circular disc (usually black and white) lowered into water. The depth at which it disappears from view gives the Secchi depth — a measure of water clarity (turbidity).

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The process of nitrification in the nitrogen cycle involves
options: bacteria converting atmospheric nitrogen to ammonia
bacteria converting ammonia to nitrites and then nitrates
plants absorbing nitrates from the soil
bacteria converting nitrates to nitrogen gas
heldExamples.explanation: Nitrification is carried out by nitrifying bacteria: Nitrosomonas converts ammonia (NH3) to nitrites (NO2-), and Nitrobacter converts nitrites to nitrates (NO3-), making nitrogen available to plants.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The most effective way to control malaria in a community is to
options: vaccinate all inhabitants against the disease
eliminate the vector by draining stagnant water and using insecticides
treat all cases of fever with antibiotics
ban movement of people between regions
heldExamples.explanation: Vector control — eliminating mosquito breeding sites (draining stagnant water, clearing vegetation), using insecticide-treated bed nets, and indoor spraying — is the most effective malaria control strategy.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: In a cross between two heterozygous tall plants (Tt x Tt), what is the expected phenotypic ratio in the offspring?
heldExamples.explanation: Tt x Tt produces TT : 2Tt : tt (genotypic ratio 1:2:1). Phenotypically, TT and Tt are both tall (T is dominant), giving 3 tall : 1 short.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Sickle cell anaemia is caused by
options: a point mutation resulting in the substitution of glutamic acid by valine in haemoglobin
a dominant allele on the X chromosome
the absence of a sex chromosome
heldExamples.explanation: Sickle cell anaemia results from a single base change (point mutation) in the HBB gene, causing the 6th amino acid of the beta-globin chain to change from glutamic acid to valine. This produces HbS, which polymerises at low oxygen tensions, distorting red blood cells into a sickle shape.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Which of the following techniques has been used to produce human insulin for diabetics using genetic engineering?
options: Insertion of the human insulin gene into bacterial DNA (recombinant DNA technology)
Chemical synthesis of insulin from amino acids in a laboratory only
heldExamples.explanation: Recombinant DNA technology (genetic engineering) involves inserting the human insulin gene into Escherichia coli or yeast cells. These bacteria then express the gene and produce human insulin in large quantities.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Continuous variation, such as height in a human population, is controlled by
options: a single gene with two alleles
heldExamples.explanation: Traits showing continuous variation (e.g. height, skin colour) are polygenic — controlled by many genes each with a small additive effect — and are also significantly influenced by environmental factors (nutrition, sunlight). This produces a continuous range of values.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The phenotypic ratio obtained from the cross AaBb x AaBb (dihybrid cross, both genes unlinked) is
heldExamples.explanation: When two heterozygous dihybrid parents (AaBb x AaBb) are crossed, using Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment, the phenotypic ratio is 9 (A_B_) : 3 (A_bb) : 3 (aaB_) : 1 (aabb) = 9:3:3:1.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The ability to roll the tongue (dominant) versus inability to roll the tongue (recessive) is an example of
heldExamples.explanation: Tongue rolling is a discontinuous variation — individuals either can roll their tongue or they cannot. There are no intermediates. It is controlled primarily by a single gene (though the genetics is more complex in reality).

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The concept of organic evolution is best defined as
options: the development of an individual organism from embryo to adult
the sum total of all adaptive changes in populations over long periods, resulting in diversity of life
the genetic changes within a single individual during its lifetime
the process of growth and development from birth to maturity
heldExamples.explanation: Organic evolution refers to the gradual change in heritable characteristics of biological populations over successive generations through processes such as natural selection, mutation, genetic drift, and gene flow — resulting in the diversity of all life on Earth.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Which evolutionary evidence would be considered the most direct and modern?
options: Molecular evidence — DNA, protein sequences, and genetic studies
heldExamples.explanation: Molecular evidence (DNA and protein sequence comparisons, phylogenomics) is considered the most direct modern evidence for evolution. It provides precise measurement of evolutionary distance between species and can reveal relationships not apparent from morphology or embryology.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The structure that holds the yolk in position is labelled
heldExamples.explanation: This question refers to the structure of a bird's egg. The structure that holds the yolk in position is the chalaza. Even without seeing the specific diagram, you need to know the functions of the egg parts. The chalaza acts like a spring or shock absorber, keeping the yolk centered so the developing embryo isn't damaged. Don't rush; always map structure to its biological function.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Blood vessel usually pass through the structure labelled
heldExamples.explanation: This is testing your knowledge of vertebrae structure, specifically the cervical vertebra in mammals. The vertebrarterial canals are small holes found exclusively in cervical vertebrae through which blood vessels (the vertebral arteries) pass up to the brain. The trick here is remembering that the word 'arterial' in its anatomical name gives away its vital transport function!

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The epiphytic habitat can best be described as
heldExamples.explanation: Let's break this down. 'Epi' means upon, and 'phyte' means plant. Epiphytes are plants that grow on other plants (like tall trees) for physical support so they can reach sunlight. Because their lives are spent up in the branches of trees, their habitat is specifically described as arboreal (tree-dwelling).

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: A seedling grown in the dark is likely to be
heldExamples.explanation: When a plant grows in the dark, it desperately searches for light. It grows tall, thin, and pale (yellowish) because it cannot produce the green pigment chlorophyll without sunlight. This specific physiological condition is called etiolation. It is a survival mechanism to rapidly push the shoot upward to find the sun.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The part labelled IV is the
heldExamples.explanation: Based on standard biological diagrams of an egg, one of the most prominent features surrounding the central mass is the albumen (the egg white). It provides a liquid medium containing high amounts of protein and water for the developing embryo. Always associate the albumen with hydration and protein supply for the growing chick.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The parts which function together to bring about hearing are labelled
heldExamples.explanation: This question tests your understanding of the pathway of sound in the mammalian ear. Hearing strictly requires the eardrum (tympanum) to pick up vibrations, the ear ossicles to amplify them, and the cochlea to convert these mechanical vibrations into nerve impulses. The trick here is recognizing which structures are for hearing versus which are for balance.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Carbon (IV) oxide content of the atmosphere is least affected by
options: cutting down and clearing of forests
heldExamples.explanation: Think about the carbon cycle as a delicately balanced budget. Plant and animal respiration releases carbon (IV) oxide naturally, but this is part of a continuous cycle heavily balanced out by photosynthesis. Therefore, it least affects the *net* concentration in the atmosphere. Conversely, burning fossil fuels, forest fires, and massive deforestation drastically shift this natural equilibrium.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The highest percentage of energy in an ecosystem occurs at the level of the
heldExamples.explanation: Energy flow in an ecosystem always starts at the base. Producers (green plants) trap energy directly from the sun, making them the trophic level with the highest total energy. As you move up the food chain to primary and then secondary consumers, about 90% of the energy is lost at each step as heat and through basic metabolic processes.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
heldExamples.question: A freshwater pond may contain
options: tadpole, water boatman, leeches and crab
water beetle, shrimps, water snail and water bug
water lily, fish, water scorpion and dragon larva
pond skater, water lily, shark and mosquito larva
heldExamples.explanation: This question tests your knowledge of specific aquatic biomes. A typical freshwater pond is a small, still body of water. Organisms like water lilies, freshwater fish, water scorpions, and dragonfly larvae (nymphs) are classic components of this ecosystem. The trick is to carefully spot the 'odd one out' in the other options to eliminate them.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The probability of a baby being a boy or a girl depends on the contribution of the
heldExamples.explanation: In humans, biological sex is determined by the X and Y chromosomes. A mother can only pass on an X chromosome through her egg. The father, however, has both an X and a Y chromosome. Therefore, the sex of the baby is entirely dependent on whether the father's sex cell (sperm) fertilizing the egg happens to carry an X chromosome (making a girl) or a Y chromosome (making a boy).

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Darwin is considered the first scientist who correctly explained the theory of
heldExamples.explanation: Charles Darwin is famous for proposing the theory of organic evolution by means of natural selection. He explained how species change biologically over time because nature selects the organisms best adapted to survive and reproduce.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Both recessive and dominant characters are found
options: on different chromosomes in the cell
at the same locus of a homologous chromosome
at different loci of a homologous chromosome
on the same chromatid in a chromosome
heldExamples.explanation: Traits are controlled by pairs of genes called alleles, which can be dominant or recessive. For these alleles to interact and determine a specific trait (like eye colour), they must be located at the exact same spot (locus) on matching pairs of chromosomes (homologous chromosomes).

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Urea formation occurs in the
heldExamples.explanation: This is a classic exam trap! While the kidney excretes urea in urine, the liver actually produces it. Through a process called deamination, the liver breaks down toxic excess amino acids into ammonia, and then quickly converts that ammonia into less toxic urea via the ornithine cycle.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Viviparity occurs mainly in the
heldExamples.explanation: Viviparity means giving birth to live young that have developed inside the mother's body, receiving nutrients directly from her (usually via a placenta). This internal development and live birth is a hallmark defining characteristic of most mammals.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
heldExamples.question: An association between the root nodule of a leguminous plant and rhizobium sp , is known as
heldExamples.explanation: The Rhizobium bacteria fix atmospheric nitrogen into a usable form for the legume, while the plant provides the bacteria with carbohydrates and a safe home in its root nodules. Since both organisms mutually benefit from living closely together, this is a classic example of symbiosis (specifically mutualism).

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The enzyme invertase will hydrolyze sucrose to give
heldExamples.explanation: Sucrose (common table sugar) is a complex sugar known as a disaccharide. When the enzyme invertase (also called sucrase) acts on it during digestion, it breaks the chemical bond to yield its two simple monosaccharide building blocks: glucose and fructose.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: When yeast respire anaerobically, it converts simple sugar to carbon (IV) oxide and
heldExamples.explanation: When yeast breaks down glucose without oxygen (anaerobic respiration or fermentation), it produces carbon (IV) oxide gas and alcohol (ethanol). This exact biological pathway is harnessed by brewers and bakers to make beer alcoholic and cause bread to rise!

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Most monocots are easily recognized by their
heldExamples.explanation: Monocotyledonous plants, such as grasses, maize, and sugar cane, typically feature long, narrow, sword-like leaves with parallel veins running along their length. In contrast, dicots usually have broader leaves with a branching network of veins.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The role of the male adult honey bee is to
heldExamples.explanation: In a highly organized honey bee colony, the male bees (called drones) have only one primary biological purpose: to fly out and fertilize a receptive queen on her mating flight. They do not have stingers, cannot forage for food, and do no work within the hive.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The mode of feeding in Amoeba and Hydra is
heldExamples.explanation: Both Amoeba (a single-celled protozoan) and Hydra (a simple multicellular animal) cannot manufacture their own food. They must feed on other ready-made organic matter in their environment. This mode of feeding, where you rely on others for nutrition, is broadly called heterotrophic nutrition.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The part labelled II is the
heldExamples.explanation: In standard JAMB diagrams of the human ear, the structures immediately following the eardrum (tympanic membrane) in the middle ear are the three tiny bones: the malleus, incus, and stapes. Collectively, these are the ear ossicles. Their job is to bridge the gap and mechanically amplify sound vibrations from the outer ear to the inner ear.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The structure above represents a
heldExamples.explanation: When dealing with vertebrae diagrams in UTME, look for defining features! A lumbar vertebra (found in the lower back) is characterized by a massive, thick centrum to support body weight, and large, wing-like transverse processes for the attachment of heavy back muscles. If you see those, it's definitely lumbar.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Amphibians are normally found
options: in water and on moist land
heldExamples.explanation: The word amphibian literally means both kinds of life. Frogs, toads, and salamanders start their lives in water (using gills) and usually move to land as adults (using lungs and skin). However, their skin must remain moist for gas exchange, and they must return to water to lay their jelly-like eggs. Thus, in water and on moist land perfectly describes their habitat.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Salts and water are absorbed in the roots and transported to leaves by
heldExamples.explanation: Water first enters the root hairs from the soil primarily by osmosis (moving from a higher water potential in the soil to a lower one in the root). Once inside, this water, along with dissolved mineral salts, is pulled upwards to the leaves through the dead, hollow tubes of the xylem tissues.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
heldExamples.question: The most important adaptation of xerophytes is the ability of the protoplasm to
options: resist being damaged by loss of water
store sugar and minerals in the vacuoles
heldExamples.explanation: Xerophytes are extreme survivors; they live in deserts where water is practically non-existent. While they have physical adaptations like thick cuticles and deep roots, their most crucial internal, physiological adaptation is having a specialized protoplasm that can tolerate severe desiccation (drying out) without dying, allowing the plant to revive when rains finally come.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Which of following groups is the most advanced?
heldExamples.explanation: To find the most advanced group, we look at the evolutionary timeline of plants: algae (Thallophytes) came first, then mosses (Bryophytes), then ferns (Pteridophytes), and finally seed-bearing plants (Gymnosperms and Angiosperms). Gymnosperms are the most advanced here because they reproduce using seeds (which protect the embryo) rather than simple spores, and they have fully developed vascular tissues.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
heldExamples.question: The veins of the leaf are formed by the
heldExamples.explanation: When you look at the veins running through a leaf, you are actually looking at the plant's plumbing system! These veins are structurally made of vascular bundles, which contain the xylem (for bringing water up) and the phloem (for carrying sugars away).

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The number of plants species obtained from a population study of a garden is as follows: Guinea grass (15), Ipomea spp (5), sida spp (7) and Imperata spp (23). What is the percentage of occurrence of Imperata spp ?
heldExamples.explanation: This is a simple frequency calculation. First, find the total number of all plants: 15 + 5 + 7 + 23 = 50 total plants. Next, divide the number of Imperata spp (23) by the total (50), and multiply by 100 to get the percentage. The math is: (23 / 50) x 100 = 46%. Don't rush the arithmetic!

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
heldExamples.question: The distribution of plants in a rain forest is governed mainly by
heldExamples.explanation: While it is called a rain forest, rainfall is abundant and continuous everywhere in this biome. Therefore, water is not the limiting factor. Because the tree canopy is so incredibly thick, the major fierce competition among plants is for the limited sunlight filtering down. This competition for light creates the distinct stratification (layers) seen in rainforests.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
heldExamples.question: The ability of an organism to live successfully in an environment is known as
heldExamples.explanation: Survival in a specific environment relies on the organism having suitable biological characteristics to cope with those specific conditions. This possession or adjustment of traits (whether physical or behavioral) that allows an organism to thrive is precisely defined as adaptation.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Water fleas, wood lice and barnacles belong to the group?
heldExamples.explanation: These organisms are all jointed-legged invertebrates (arthropods) that are primarily adapted to aquatic or highly moist environments. The defining trait tying them together (even the terrestrial woodlouse) is that they possess two pairs of antennae and breathe using gills or gill-like structures, which places them squarely in the class Crustacea.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The factor that least affects food shortages in sub-saharan Africa is
heldExamples.explanation: You have to read the question carefully here — it asks what least affects (causes) food shortages. Mixed-cropping is an advanced agricultural technique where different complementary crops are planted together. It actually improves soil fertility, maximizes land use, and prevents total crop failure, thereby actively reducing food shortages! The other options are destructive forces.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The greatest influence on a stable ecosystem in nature is exerted by
heldExamples.explanation: While natural abiotic and biotic factors shape ecosystems, human beings (man) exert the most rapid, drastic, and often irreversible influence. Through large-scale agriculture, deforestation, industrialization, and urbanization, human activity can permanently alter or destroy a stable ecosystem faster than any other natural environmental force.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The transportation of oxygen and carbon (IV) oxide in mammals is carried out by
heldExamples.explanation: Erythrocytes (red blood cells) are biologically designed for gas transport. They lack a nucleus to make room for hemoglobin, an iron-containing protein that binds beautifully with oxygen (forming oxyhemoglobin) and can also carry a portion of carbon (IV) oxide back to the lungs. No other blood cell performs this transport role.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Which of the following is likely to encourage inbreeding in plants?
heldExamples.explanation: Inbreeding in plants occurs through self-pollination. A hermaphrodite (bisexual) flower is built with both the male stamen and female pistil housed together inside the very same flower. Because they share such a tight physical space, it is incredibly easy for the flower's own pollen to simply fall onto its own stigma, heavily encouraging inbreeding.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: When specimen X is mixed with few drops of iodine solution, the appearance of a blue-black colour confirms that X is
heldExamples.explanation: This is the classic, definitive biochemical test for starch! Iodine solution is naturally a yellowish-brown color. However, when it interacts with the complex, spiraled molecular structure of starch, it slips inside the coils and instantly produces a deep blue-black color complex.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The physical space occupied by an organism together with its functional role in community can be described as
heldExamples.explanation: While its physical address is its habitat, an organism's profession (what it eats, what eats it, its active times, and how it interacts with the environment) combined with that space forms its complete ecological niche.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: In a field experiment, the frequency of water leaf was observed to be 48 after 20 tosses of a 2m\(^2\) quadrat. What is the density of the plants in the field?
heldExamples.explanation: The question asks for density, which is number of individuals per unit area. The total area sampled = 20 quadrats × 2 m² = 40 m². If the frequency (number of occurrences) is 48, then density = 48 / 40 = 1.2 per m². The trick is to recognise that 'frequency' here refers to total counts, not a percentage.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Insects are considered the most successful among the invertebrates because they?
options: possess the ability to change their forms
heldExamples.explanation: The question asks why insects are the most successful invertebrates. While they have exoskeletons and wings, their success is primarily due to their ability to survive in diverse habitats (from deserts to water) and their high reproductive capacity. Option B captures this broad adaptability.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: A state in Nigeria that is most susceptible to desert encroachment is
heldExamples.explanation: Desert encroachment (desertification) is most severe in the northernmost states of Nigeria that border the Sahel. Katsina is a northern state that is highly susceptible to desertification. Kwara, Taraba, and Kaduna are less affected as they are further south or have more vegetation.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Which of the following is an example of intraspecific competition?
options: a lizard and an ant-eater chasing an insect
a worker termite and a soldier in a limited space.
a hawk and an eagle targeting the same chicken
yam and potato shots growing out through the same window
heldExamples.explanation: Intraspecific competition is between organisms of the same species. Yam and potato shoots are different species, but here both are plants competing for space and light – however, the question considers them as individuals competing for the same resources. The other options involve different species (interspecific competition).

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Plants survive hot dry conditions by
options: storing water in large parenchyma cells
heldExamples.explanation: Xerophytes (desert plants) store water in specialized parenchyma tissue in stems or leaves (e.g., succulents). Producing numerous leaves and having numerous stomata would increase water loss; evergreen leaves lose water throughout the year and are not a xerophytic adaptation.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The soil type that will be most difficult to plough in a wet season is one that is
heldExamples.explanation: Clay soil has very fine particles that become sticky and waterlogged when wet, making it extremely difficult to plough. Sandy soil is loose and easy to work, loam is ideal, and silt is intermediate.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The absence of special food and water-conducting systems restricts the body size in
heldExamples.explanation: Algae, liverworts, and mosses lack true vascular tissue (xylem and phloem), so they rely on diffusion for transport, limiting their size. Ferns and other pteridophytes have vascular tissue and can grow larger.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The anaerobic fermentation of a glucose molecule yields
heldExamples.explanation: Anaerobic fermentation of glucose (as in yeast) produces ethanol (alcohol) and carbon dioxide, with a net gain of 2 ATP molecules. 38 ATP is from aerobic respiration; pyruvic acid is an intermediate; water and CO2 are products of aerobic respiration.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Rodents gnaw on food with their
heldExamples.explanation: Rodents have large, continuously growing incisors that are chisel-shaped and adapted for gnawing. Molars are for grinding, strong jaws are general, and flat-ridged teeth are typical of herbivores like cattle.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The scarcity of food causes a sudden decrease in population size by
heldExamples.explanation: When food becomes scarce, individuals starve, leading to increased mortality (death rate), which directly reduces population size. Reproductive rate may also decrease, but the immediate effect is mortality. Immigration would increase population, and competition is not minimized.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Epigeal germination of a seed is characterized by
options: more rapid elongation of the hypocotyl than the epicotyl
more rapid elongation of the epicotyl than the hypocotyl
equal growth of both the hypocotyl and epicotyl
lack of growth of the hypocotyl
heldExamples.explanation: In epigeal germination, the hypocotyl (the stem below the cotyledons) elongates rapidly, pushing the cotyledons above the ground. In hypogeal germination, the epicotyl elongates and the cotyledons remain below ground.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Nervous control differs from hormonal control in that the former
heldExamples.explanation: Nervous control produces rapid, short-lived responses, while hormonal control is slower but longer-lasting. Nervous transmission involves both electrical and chemical signals (at synapses), has specific pathways (neurons), and is not a 'lower' process.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The opening of the stoma is controlled by the
options: increase in solute concentration in the guard cells
decrease in solute concentration in the guard cells
heldExamples.explanation: Stomata open when the solute concentration in guard cells increases, causing water to enter by osmosis. This makes the guard cells turgid and they bow outward, opening the pore. A decrease in solute concentration causes water to leave, making them flaccid and closing the pore.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The progressive loss of energy at each level in a food chain leads to
options: an increase in biomas at each successive level
a decrease in biomass at each successive level
an increase in the number of organism at each successive level
an increase in the total number of organisms at  each successive level
heldExamples.explanation: As energy flows through a food chain, about 90% is lost as heat at each trophic level. This results in less energy available to support biomass at higher levels, so biomass decreases progressively from producers to top consumers.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Sex - linked genes are located on
heldExamples.explanation: Sex-linked genes are located on the X chromosome. The Y chromosome has few genes. Traits like colour blindness and haemophilia are X-linked. While some genes are on the Y (Y-linked), the term 'sex-linked' typically refers to X-linked inheritance.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: A plant-like feature in Euglena is the
heldExamples.explanation: Euglena has a pigment spot (eyespot) that detects light, which is a plant-like feature as it helps the organism move towards light for photosynthesis (like plants do). The pellicle is a protein layer (animal-like), and the gullet is for ingestion (animal-like).

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: All living cells require water because it
options: is a medium for all metabolic reactions
is a medium that neutralizes the acids in cells
is the main source of energy for the cell
prevents the development of dieseases in cells
heldExamples.explanation: Water is the universal solvent and medium in which all metabolic reactions occur. It also transports nutrients and removes wastes. It does not neutralize acids significantly, is not an energy source (glucose is), and does not directly prevent diseases.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
heldExamples.question: In the internal structure of plants, a wide pith in the centre is common to
heldExamples.explanation: A wide pith is characteristic of dicot roots and monocot stems. Dicot stems often have a pith but it is not always wide; monocot roots have a central pith or parenchyma. This question tests the specific arrangement of tissues in different plant organs.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The surface of an alveolus in a mammal is well supplied with tiny blood vessels known as
heldExamples.explanation: Alveoli are surrounded by a dense network of capillaries, which are the smallest blood vessels where gas exchange occurs. Arterioles are small arteries, venules are small veins, and arteries are larger vessels; capillaries are the specific site of exchange.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Identical twins inherit their genes from
heldExamples.explanation: Identical (monozygotic) twins develop from a single fertilized egg (zygote) that splits into two embryos. They share the same genetic material because they come from the same egg and sperm. Fraternal twins come from two different eggs and sperms.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The larval stage of a mosquito is called
heldExamples.explanation: The larval stage of a mosquito is called a wriggler, which is aquatic and moves with a wriggling motion. Grub is the larva of beetles, maggot is the larva of flies, and caterpillar is the larva of butterflies and moths.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: If a nursing mother is not producing enough milk, her hormonal system is probably deficient in
heldExamples.explanation: Prolactin is the hormone responsible for milk production (lactation) in mammals. Testosterone is a male sex hormone, thyroxin regulates metabolism, and insulin regulates blood sugar. Deficiency in prolactin would reduce milk production.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The breakdown of fats and oils into simpler absorbable compounds is catalyzed by the group of enzymes called
heldExamples.explanation: Lipases are enzymes that break down lipids (fats and oils) into fatty acids and glycerol. Hydrolases are a broad group that catalyze hydrolysis reactions (including lipases), amylases digest starch, and peptidases digest proteins.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: An evidence of the relationship between living organisms and their extinct relatives can best be obtained from
heldExamples.explanation: Palaeontology is the study of fossils, which provides direct evidence of extinct organisms and their relationship to living ones. Embryology, comparative anatomy, and physiology provide indirect evidence of evolution through similarities and differences, but fossils are the most direct evidence of extinct forms.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The population density of Tridex in an abandoned square farm land of side 200 m was found to be 5 plants per m\(^2\). The population size of the plant on the farm is
heldExamples.explanation: The farm is square with side 200 m, so the area = 200 m × 200 m = 40,000 m². Population density is 5 plants per m². Total population size = density × area = 5 × 40,000 = 200,000 plants. Many students may forget to square the side length, leading to the wrong answer.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The average number of individuals of a species per unit area of the habitat is the?
heldExamples.explanation: Population density describes how many individuals of a species occur within a given unit area. The key clue is per unit area: number of individuals divided by the area occupied.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
heldExamples.question: The activity of an organism which affects the survival of another organism in the same habitat constitutes?
heldExamples.explanation: A biotic factor is an effect arising from living organisms. Competition, predation, parasitism and disease are examples because one organism can influence the survival or distribution of another.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
heldExamples.question: Which of the following organisms is mainly found in the marine habitat?
heldExamples.explanation: Dogfish are sharks and are marine animals, meaning they live primarily in salt-water environments. Achatina and tortoises are terrestrial, while the common tilapia is mainly associated with freshwater habitats.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: In the male reproductive system of a mammal, sperm is stored in the?
heldExamples.explanation: The epididymis is the coiled tube attached to each testis where sperm mature and are temporarily stored. The seminiferous tubules produce sperm, while the vas deferens transports mature sperm away from the epididymis.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The loss of soil through erosion can be reduced by?
heldExamples.explanation: Crop rotation helps maintain vegetation cover and improves soil structure, reducing the amount of exposed soil that can be washed or blown away. The key idea is that good land management reduces soil vulnerability to erosion.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The outer layer of the kidney where the Bowman's capsules are found is the?
heldExamples.explanation: Bowman's capsules are located in the renal cortex, the outer region of the kidney. They surround the glomeruli and form the beginning of the nephron, where filtration of blood occurs.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Which of the following groups of cells is devoid of true nuclei?
heldExamples.explanation: Members of Monera, such as bacteria, are prokaryotic and therefore lack a membrane-bound true nucleus. Their genetic material lies in a nucleoid region rather than inside a nuclear membrane.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the nucleus of a cell?
options: it translates genetic information for the manufacture of proteins
it stores and carries hereditary information
it is reservoir of energy for the cell
it controls the life processes of the cell
heldExamples.explanation: The nucleus stores genetic information and regulates cell activities through control of gene expression. It is not an energy reservoir; ATP is the immediate energy currency of the cell, while mitochondria are major sites of ATP production.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The sheet of muscle that separates the thoracic and the abdominal cavities is the?
heldExamples.explanation: The diaphragm is a dome-shaped sheet of muscle separating the thoracic cavity from the abdominal cavity. Its contraction and relaxation change the volume of the thoracic cavity, making it essential for breathing.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Thyroxine and adrenalin are examples of hormones which control?
heldExamples.explanation: Thyroxine influences metabolic activity and nervous-system function, while adrenaline produces rapid physiological changes associated with emergency responses. Together, these hormones can influence behavioural and physiological responses rather than inherited traits such as blood group or tongue-rolling ability.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Circulation of blood to all parts of the body except the lungs is through?
heldExamples.explanation: Systemic circulation carries blood between the heart and the rest of the body, excluding the lungs. The left side of the heart pumps oxygenated blood through the aorta to body tissues, while systemic veins return deoxygenated blood to the right side of the heart.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The oily substance that lubricates the mammalian hair to keep it flexible and water repellent is secreted by the?
heldExamples.explanation: Sebaceous glands secrete sebum, an oily substance that lubricates the hair and skin. Sebum helps prevent excessive drying and contributes to making the hair more flexible and water resistant.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Low annual rainfall, sparse vegetation, high diurnal temperatures and cold nights are characteristic features of the?
heldExamples.explanation: Deserts receive very little rainfall and therefore support sparse vegetation. Their dry atmosphere also allows large temperature differences between hot days and cold nights.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: An animal body that can be cut along its axis in any plane to give two identical parts is said to be
heldExamples.explanation: Radial symmetry means the body can be divided into similar halves through several planes passing through its central axis. Bilateral symmetry allows division into matching halves through only one particular plane.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.topic: Internal structure of plants and animals
heldExamples.question: Plants that show secondary growth are usually found among the
heldExamples.explanation: Secondary growth is the increase in thickness of stems and roots, mainly through the activity of lateral meristems such as vascular cambium and cork cambium. It is characteristic of most dicotyledonous woody plants, whereas most monocots do not undergo typical secondary growth.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: Which of the following is most advanced in the evolutionary trend of animals?
heldExamples.explanation: Among these organisms, the cockroach represents the most advanced level of organization in the evolutionary sequence traditionally taught in the UTME syllabus. It has a well-developed body organization, including specialized organs and organ systems.

heldExamples.subject: Biology
heldExamples.question: The feature that links birds to reptiles in evolution is the possession of
heldExamples.explanation: Birds are linked evolutionarily with reptiles by several shared features, including scales on their legs and feet. Feathers and beaks are characteristic bird adaptations, while a skeleton is too general to establish the specific relationship.
